author: imdbfan-5737377658
title: Disney's Snow White Falls Flat
text:
I went into Disney's new live-action Snow White remake expecting big things, but what I got was one of the most disappointing films I've ever had the misfortune of sitting through. As much as I understand the need for a new take on an old favorite story, this adaptation goes so far off the map from the center of the original that it's barely even the same story anymore. From bad choices in story to subpar acting, this film is a complete letdown.

To begin with, the script is a catastrophe. Instead of sticking to the timeless fairy tale, the makers of the movie decided to inject time-worn contemporary themes that end up feeling imposed and not natural. Snow White has been a story of compassion, determination, and the triumph of good over evil, but this retelling strips the magic from it and replaces it with clichéd and unoriginal dialogue. All the magic, the whimsy, and emotional richness that rendered the animated film classic so a gem are here.

Even the performances fail to stem the disappointment. The leading actress lacks presence strong enough to service such a larger-than-life figure, serving up a lifeless and indifferent performance. Snow White is intended as a warm, innocent character here she comes off as mundane and uninspirational. The cast chemistry is non-existent, which makes it difficult to believe in any of the relationships. The villain, usually a standout in any Disney film, is reduced to an afterthought of a caricature and lacks the menace and grandeur of the original Evil Queen.

Visually, the film is underwhelming too. Disney is known for gorgeous cinematography and top-notch special effects, and this film falls far short of that. The CGI is spotty, with some of the scenes being partially done or looking overly artificial. The costume design, an opportunity to pay respect to the original while adding new creative energy, is uninspired and dull. The setting, which should resemble a magical fairy tale world, feels instead stale and lifeless.

Perhaps the most disappointing is the music-or, rather, the lack of memorable music. The original Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs had a soundtrack full of classic songs that have stood the test of time. This one, though, fails to create any really magical musical moments. The few that are there are forgettable, lacking the emotional resonance and charm of the classic tunes. The decision to cut or recreate beloved songs was a basic flaw that removes a critical level of nostalgia and emotional impact.

Even the seven dwarfs, one of the greatest things about the original film, are ruined. Their personality, charm, and humor are stripped away and replaced with flat characters that serve no purpose in the story. Instead of being a highlight, they are an afterthought, and it is surprising given how integral they are to the story.

This movie fails overall as both an actual adaptation and as a quality film in itself. It lacks all the heart, charm, and magic that made the original so integral to our culture. Instead, it's cynical, soulless attempt at cashing in on nostalgia and disregarding what made the story work in the first place. Disney has had some success with live-action remakes in the past, but Snow White is a case in point of what happens when a studio prioritizes following trends over conveying a good story.

If you're a fan of the original, I'd recommend skipping this entirely. It's a waste of time, a waste of potential, and a complete disappointment. Hopefully, Disney will learn from this failure and start treating their classics with the respect they deserve. Until then, I'll be rewatching the 1937 animated masterpiece to cleanse my palate. This was one of disneys biggest mistakes highly do not recommend.

I recently had the pleasure of watching A Minecraft Movie with my family, and it was an absolute delight from start to finish. The film is a vibrant, family-friendly adventure that perfectly captures the essence of the beloved video game. Even as someone who isn't a gamer, I found myself thoroughly entertained by the movie's infectious energy and humor.
One of the standout aspects of the film is its attention to detail. The creators have woven in numerous Easter eggs and references that will delight both casual viewers and hardcore Minecraft fans. From the meticulously crafted environments to the creative use of Minecraft elements like crafting tables and mobs, every scene is filled with visual nods that add depth and charm to the story. The film's portrayal of the Overworld, with its blocky landscapes and colorful creatures, is visually stunning and immersive.

author: shashanksingh-57363
title: Absolute Cinema
text: The *Minecraft Movie* is a mixed bag that shines brightest for fans of the game, especially younger audiences. While critics have pointed out its lackluster story and uneven character development, the film excels in faithfully recreating Minecraft's blocky universe with stunning visuals and countless Easter eggs. Jack Black's portrayal of Steve brings humor and charm, and the movie thrives when showcasing the limitless creativity of Minecraft's world. Though it may not appeal to all, its playful tone and game-inspired moments make it an enjoyable experience for die-hard fans and families alike.

author: dxrhvybb
title: The cast, why they took the cast so seriously low?
text:
I went in expecting a classic Disney story, something that would bring back the magic I loved as a child. Instead, I got a lifeless performance, horrible acting, and a film that seemed to lack care in even the smallest details. At first, I thought I was alone in feeling this way-but clearly, I wasn't.
Rachel Zegler, in a role that many actresses would have given anything to play, delivers a shockingly dull and uninspired performance as Snow White. While she has a strong singing voice, that's where the praise ends. Her acting is flat, completely missing the warmth and charm that made the animated character so iconic. Her line delivery feels robotic, her emotions forced, and she never manages to bring any real depth to the role. Instead of capturing Snow White's innocence and kindness, she comes across as detached, uninterested, and, at times, completely disconnected from the character.
What a complete waste of time.

author: rieshamilton
title: Best film of all time
text: From the moment the opening scene lit up the screen, I knew The Minecraft Movie was going to be something truly special. As a longtime fan of the game, I went in with high hopes-but what I experienced was beyond anything I could have imagined. This film isn't just a video game adaptation; it's a love letter to the creativity, adventure, and endless possibilities that Minecraft represents. It's a thrilling, heartwarming, and visually stunning journey that captures the essence of the game while telling a story that resonates with both die-hard fans and newcomers alike. A Faithful Yet Fresh Take on the Minecraft Universe One of my biggest worries was whether the movie would stay true to the spirit of Minecraft while still offering something new. I'm thrilled to say it absolutely does! The world-building is phenomenal-every blocky tree, every creeper lurking in the shadows, every sprawling biome feels like it was pulled straight from the game, yet expanded in ways that make the universe feel alive. The attention to detail is astounding, from the iconic sound effects (that "ssss" still terrifies me) to the way characters craft tools and build structures in real-time. The story is a perfect blend of adventure, humor, and emotion. Without spoiling anything, it follows a group of unlikely heroes-some familiar faces and some new-as they embark on an epic quest to save their world from a looming threat. The pacing is fantastic, balancing intense action sequences with quieter, heartfelt moments that give the characters real depth. And yes, there are plenty of Easter eggs and references that will have fans grinning from ear to ear. Stellar Voice Acting and Characters You'll Love The casting is spot-on. Every voice actor brings their character to life with so much personality and charm. Steve (played by an incredibly talented actor) is everything we hoped for-stoic yet expressive, brave yet relatable. The supporting cast, including a hilarious parrot sidekick and a surprisingly complex villain, adds so much flavor to the story. Even the mobs-zombies, skeletons, and of course, the ever-menacing Ender Dragon-are given moments to shine in ways that feel fresh and exciting. Visual Spectacle - Blocky Beauty Brought to Life The animation style is a perfect marriage of Minecraft's signature blocky aesthetic and cinematic polish. The way light filters through leaves, water flows dynamically, and explosions send blocks flying is nothing short of breathtaking. The action sequences are fluid and exhilarating, especially a climactic battle that had me on the edge of my seat. And the Nether and End dimensions? Absolutely stunning-vibrant, dangerous, and full of surprises. A Soundtrack That Hits All the Right Notes The music is a beautiful mix of nostalgic Minecraft melodies and sweeping orchestral pieces that elevate every scene. Hearing those iconic C418-inspired tunes reimagined with a full cinematic score gave me chills. title: Fair but stale!

Now, Gal Gadot (oh boy) plays a flowy and way too over the top Evil Queen, that unfortunately is but a far dying echo of the Evil Queen in the animation.
Production problems and reshoots can be clearly seen when Snow White's hair distractingly changes both length and style, sometimes in the very same music sequence.
Speaking of music sequence, the Evil Queen absolutely did not need songs of her own, what breaks her character and makes us lose credibility in her evilness. She just feels...goofy.
I personally also felt a slight little political theme here and there, but that might just be me.
That being said, again the movie is not bad. It's CUTE and endearing but a little stale, like a cookie that's not very well baked, but it still ok. The visuals and CGI are stunning and, yes, I can see some uncanny valley happening with the dwarfes but nothing distracting or creepy at all. author: mitchellrath
title: A Minecraft Movie: Film Review
text:
Released 10 days ago (April 4th), A Minecraft Movie has created the following: laughs, controversy, and big bucks. As of April 14th, A Minecraft Movie has earned over half a billion dollars at the box office and is going into Easter weekend with that number only going up. Who knew a simple sandbox game about creating wonders during the day and dodging zombies by night would be a hit at the theaters. With the unlikely duo in the star roles, Jack Black (playing Steve) and Jason Momoa (playing a character known as Garrett "The Garbage Man" Garrison) set off on an adventure within the Overworld to save the villagers from the gold-hungry antagonist Malgosha (voiced by Rachel House). Together Steve and "The Garbage Man" are joined by other human characters Natalie, Sebastian, and Dawn. All together they will explore the land, explore the world, and build forts and weapons.
This will go without saying; however, those audience members who have never heard, or played, Minecraft will have no idea what is going on. On top of the ridiculous humor, and Jack Black over-the-top personality, this movie will fly right by you and leave you wondering, "what did I just see?". As for myself, I am a Minecraft novice, I was able to notice most of the game references. As for the most talked about moment, yes, I mean the "Chicken Jockey", that reference went over my head. Back on track, fans of the Minecraft game will appreciate the film's attention to detail and loyalty to the source material.
Most of the dialogue throughout the film tries extremely hard to make the audience laugh. Granted, this film is a comedy inside an outrageous premise. The tactic of "let's lean into the ridiculousness" is what is showcased. I'll admit, a few parts gave me a few good chuckles and two good laughs. The humor earned a hard PG rating and possibly going into PG-13. At the end of the day, this film is fun, and I unexpectedly had a good time. The heavy use of green screen is justified given the Overworld context. Nevertheless, I liked how the movie looked overall. It communicates exactly what you're going to get. Ridiculous, stupid laughs.
Overall, both fans of Minecraft and comedy will appreciate this movie. Maybe convince a few people to give Minecraft to try to see what it is all about. With a runtime of 1 hour and 41 minutes, you can expect a good old ridiculous time with this film. I would give this film a 6/10.

author: imdbfan-7365666712
title: Really Bad Movie
text:
I went into this film hoping for a fresh yet faithful take on Snow White, but what I got was a soulless, uninspired mess that completely misses the charm, heart, and magic of the original. Disney's attempt to modernize this beloved fairy tale resulted in a film that feels neither nostalgic nor innovative-it simply feels empty.
A Lead Character That Lacks Charm
One of the biggest issues with this adaptation is Snow White herself. The character in the original story was known for her kindness, innocence, and warmth-qualities that made her beloved by the dwarfs and the audience alike. In this version, however, she is rewritten into a completely different person, and not in a good way. Instead of a kind-hearted and gentle protagonist, we get a self-righteous, almost arrogant version of Snow White who lacks any real charm. There is no sense of wonder or joy in her journey, and she doesn't feel like a character you want to root for.
The performance also leaves much to be desired. There is no depth, no warmth, and no real emotional range. Every line delivery feels forced and unnatural, making it hard to connect with her character. It's a shame because a strong lead performance could have salvaged some of the film's weaker moments.
Where is the Magic?
Disney built its empire on telling magical, timeless stories, but this film has none of that. The whimsical atmosphere that made the original so enchanting is completely absent. The visuals are bland, the cinematography is uninspired, and even the fantasy elements feel generic. Instead of the rich, colorful world we expect from a Snow White adaptation, we get a film that looks strangely dull and lifeless.
The lack of effort in the CGI is another huge letdown. The creatures and backgrounds often look artificial and unfinished, making it hard to feel immersed in the world. When you compare this to Disney's past live-action films, the drop in quality is shocking. It's as if the studio didn't even try to create something visually memorable.
The Dwarfs Are an Afterthought
One of the most beloved aspects of the original Snow White is the seven dwarfs, each with their own distinct personality and charm. In this version, however, they are almost irrelevant. Instead of being integral to the story, they feel like last-minute additions that serve no real purpose. Their interactions with Snow White lack warmth and humor, and there is no real emotional bond between them.
This is one of the biggest disappointments of the film because the dwarfs added so much heart and comedy to the original. Without them, the movie feels even more lifeless.
The Villain is Forgettable
A great Disney movie needs a great villain, but the Evil Queen in this version is nothing special. In the animated classic, she was terrifying, elegant, and truly menacing. Here, she is just... there. She lacks any real presence or threat, and her motivations are vague at best. A weak villain makes for a weak story, and unfortunately, this.

title: A Minecraft Movie, Not The Minecraft Movie

author: calebcollier-63164
title: A Blockbuster Triumph
text:
As a devoted fan of the Minecraft universe, I approached "A Minecraft Movie" with both excitement and a hint of skepticism. However, the film not only met but exceeded my expectations, delivering an experience that was both nostalgic and refreshingly original.
From the outset, the movie immerses viewers in the pixelated charm of the Overworld. The attention to detail in replicating the game's iconic landscapes and creatures is commendable, making it feel as though the game has come to life on the big screen.
The storyline is engaging, following four misfits who are unexpectedly transported into the Minecraft universe. Their journey of adaptation and discovery mirrors the experiences many players have had when first delving into the game. The inclusion of an expert crafter as their guide adds depth and authenticity to their adventure.
The casting is spot-on. Jack Black's portrayal of Steve is both humorous and heartfelt, capturing the essence of a seasoned Minecraft player. Jason Momoa brings a charismatic presence to the screen, and the chemistry among the ensemble cast enhances the film's dynamic.
Visually, the film is a masterpiece. The blend of live-action and CGI is seamless, staying true to the game's aesthetic while adding cinematic flair. The action sequences are thrilling, and the creative use of crafting and building pays homage to the core mechanics of Minecraft.
Moreover, the film doesn't shy away from the game's underlying themes of creativity, teamwork, and perseverance. These messages are woven naturally into the narrative, resonating with audiences of all ages.
In conclusion, "A Minecraft Movie" is a triumphant adaptation that honors its source material while crafting its own unique identity. It's a must-watch for fans and a delightful introduction for newcomers. A solid 10/10 in my book.

author: lijppie
title: Snow White and the Seven Catastrophes
text:
Once upon a time, in a land where Hollywood still understood storytelling, Snow White was a beloved fairy tale about beauty, magic, and the perils of vanity. Fast forward to today, and we now have this-a cinematic train wreck that takes a pickaxe to nostalgia and buries it in an unmarked grave.
Let's start with the most baffling issue: the Evil Queen is more beautiful than Snow White. That's not just a nitpick; it obliterates the entire premise. Why is she jealous? Does she have self-esteem issues? Did her magic mirror get hacked? Watching this film, you'd think the real villain is common sense itself.
Then there's the protagonist. Now, I don't care who plays Snow White, but at the very least, make the story make sense. The original description-skin as white as snow, lips as red as blood, hair as black as ebony-isn't just some throwaway line; it's the reason the story exists. Ignoring that detail makes it feel like the writers skimmed the Wikipedia summary and said, "Eh, close enough." Spoiler: It wasn't.
The film is also hilariously devoid of charm. No whimsy, no heart, just a dull, self-important slog that takes itself way too seriously while simultaneously treating the source material like garbage. It's like watching a birthday clown perform Shakespeare-awkward, painful, and fundamentally wrong.
The only joy I got from this experience was the memes mocking it, which ironically had more creativity than the entire film. If you want to enjoy Snow White, do yourself a favor: stick to the animated classic or, better yet, just stare at a blank wall for two hours. You'll get the same amount of plot development, but at least you won't leave feeling personally attacked.

author: ChngH
title: Blockbuster Brilliance: The Minecraft Movie Hits All the Right Chunks
text:
The Minecraft Movie is an absolute triumph, a 10/10 masterpiece that brings the iconic game to life with stunning creativity and heart. From the moment it begins, the film captures the essence of Minecraft's blocky, boundless world and transforms it into a visually spectacular adventure that's both nostalgic and fresh. The attention to detail-crisp pixelated landscapes, vibrant biomes, and perfectly crafted mobs-makes every frame a love letter to fans.
The cast is phenomenal. Jack Black's portrayal of Steve is a standout, blending rugged charm with heartfelt humor, making him the perfect everyman hero. Jason Momoa and Danielle Brooks bring depth and charisma to their roles, while the ensemble chemistry feels like a well-coordinated multiplayer session. The story strikes a brilliant balance: it's packed with thrilling action (think epic Nether showdowns) and a surprisingly touching narrative about creativity, teamwork, and survival.
What sets this movie apart is its ability to appeal to everyone-longtime players will geek out over Easter eggs like the crafting table sequences, while newcomers will be swept away by the universal appeal of its underdog spirit. The pacing is spot-on, the soundtrack bangs, and the humor lands without ever feeling forced. It's a rare adaptation that doesn't just live up to the source material-it elevates it. The Minecraft Movie is a must-see, a joyous celebration of imagination that leaves you buzzing with excitement long after the credits roll.

author: demonxcros
title: Disenchanted Mess
text: My girlfriend, a big fan of the original Snow White, wanted to see this, so we did. I had no expectations going in, but somehow still left disappointed. She didn't quite fit the role, and the writing didn't do her any favors, but she did what she could with the material. Her singing was a highlight, even though the new songs were uninspired and forgettable, she delivered them well. Her accent slipped into American in a few spots, but it wasn't too distracting. author: Gladior
title: Minecraft Movie Review - Honest Thoughts from a Longtime Player
text:
As someone who's been playing Minecraft consistently since 2019 and still enjoys hopping into servers today, I came into this movie with a mix of excitement and curiosity. I love Minecraft, and I wanted to see how they'd bring its world to life. Unfortunately, I left the theater feeling like it was a missed opportunity.
The Good:
Let's be fair-this movie is definitely designed with kids in mind. The animation is colorful, the pacing is fast, and there are plenty of goofy moments to keep younger audiences entertained. It has the spirit of Minecraft in a few places, especially visually. So if you're under 10, or watching with younger siblings, it's probably a good time.
The Not-So-Great:
1. Lack of Game Accuracy
One of the biggest letdowns is how little effort was put into staying true to how Minecraft actually works. For example, there are made-up potions that stop pigs from turning into zombified versions-something that doesn't exist in the game at all. It just feels like the writers made up random ideas without considering how the real mechanics work.
2. Water Bucket Clutch Fail
If you're going to include something like a water bucket clutch-an iconic Minecraft trick-at least get it right! In the movie, it was portrayed in a way that totally ignores how it works in the game. It's not just about pouring water while falling; it takes precision and timing, and the way they showed it felt lazy and unrealistic.
3. Cringe Humor
Let's talk about the poop singing scene... why? It was awkward, out of place, and didn't add anything to the story. It felt like it was written just to get a cheap laugh out of little kids, but for anyone older, it was just cringe.
4. Missed Lore and Gameplay Opportunities
Minecraft has so much depth they could have explored-Redstone contraptions, strongholds, the End, boss battles, even the survival aspects like hunger and crafting. Instead, most of that was skipped or overly simplified in favor of random storytelling that barely scratched the surface of what makes Minecraft so fun.
Final Thoughts:
This movie is definitely not made for the longtime Minecraft community. It's a simple, silly adventure for young viewers and casual fans, but for players like me-who've spent years learning the mechanics, building in survival mode, and exploring everything Minecraft has to offer-it feels like a wasted chance to do something amazing with the source material.
Is it the worst movie ever? No. But is it overrated and underwhelming for real fans? Absolutely.

text:
This movie feels like a 1-hour-and-49-minute SNL skit that forgot to end after the first punchline. I went in with an open mind-really, I did-but by the time the credits rolled, I was left wondering who greenlit this and why they thought it was a good idea to stretch a sketch into a feature film.
The whole thing starts off with a vibe that's trying way too hard to be clever. You've got Snow White, reimagined as this edgy, modern heroine who's more about snarky one-liners than anything resembling the fairy tale we know.
It's like they handed the script to a room full of improv comics.
The dialogue's packed with pop culture jabs and self-aware winks that might've landed if they'd kept it short and sweet. But at nearly two hours? It's exhausting.
The dwarves, for example, are less characters and more walking punchlines, each one a caricature that feels ripped from a late-night parody.
The songs are catchy for about ten seconds before you realize they're just there to pad the runtime.
I get it-they wanted to flip the script, make it fresh, appeal to a new crowd. But there's a difference between reinventing a classic and turning it into a gag.
Like an SNL bit that's funny for five minutes but keeps dragging on until you're begging for the host to cut to commercial.
Look, if you're expecting a heartfelt story or even a solid satire, you're out of luck. Snow White 2025 is a marathon of smirks that forgets fairy tales are supposed to have a little magic, not just a laugh track.
I'd give it a pass unless you've got time to kill and a soft spot for overstretched comedy.

author: vicz-08744
title: Snow brown is a hammerhead eye fish
text:
Disney's live-action Snow White (2025) is not just bad-it's a complete disaster. From the moment the first scene rolls, it's clear that this remake is an uninspired, soulless attempt to modernize a classic that didn't need fixing.
The biggest issue? The story. Instead of honoring the beloved original, Disney decided to throw in unnecessary changes that feel forced and out of place. The seven dwarfs, a crucial part of the original charm, are now CGI creations that look awkward and lifeless. And let's not forget the baffling decision to replace the Prince with a new character named Jonathan, who adds absolutely nothing to the plot.
Rachel Zegler's Snow White lacks the grace and warmth of the animated classic, and while her singing is fine, her performance is bland. Meanwhile, Gal Gadot's Evil Queen is disappointingly one-note, lacking the chilling presence that made the animated version so iconic.
Visually, the movie is another letdown. The CGI is overdone, making everything look artificial and lifeless rather than magical. Even the costume design feels cheap compared to previous Disney live-action films.
Overall, Snow White (2025) is a perfect example of why not every classic needs a remake. It strips away the magic, replaces it with uninspired changes, and ultimately turns a beloved fairytale into a forgettable mess. If you're looking for nostalgia or a worthy reimagining, this isn't it.
⭐ 0.5 - A waste of time.

author: JaykoR
title: A Minecraft Movie - A Glorious, Pixelated Fever Dream
text:
A Minecraft Movie isn't just a film-it's an existential crisis made of blocks. And somehow, that's what makes it brilliant.
There's no clean storyline to hold onto. Instead, you get a whirlwind of redstone explosions, villagers chanting in low-res Latin, and a pig who may or may not be a god. The world shifts without warning-biomes blend, the laws of physics bend, and suddenly a heartfelt monologue is interrupted by someone accidentally digging straight into lava. It's chaotic. It's absurd. It's kind of perfect.
The movie captures the true essence of Minecraft: the feeling of being dropped into a limitless world with no instructions and a thousand possibilities. Characters build and destroy, form alliances, betray each other over enchanted gear, and occasionally stop to watch the sunset in a moment of unexpected stillness. It's like a server with no admin-everyone's just trying to make meaning before a creeper ruins everything.
Visually, it's stunning in the strangest way. Blocky landscapes somehow carry real emotion. A simple house made of dirt feels like home. And when the final battle erupts between a ragtag group of players and an army of skeletons riding spiders, it's not just epic-it's earned.

author: muzotime-57720
title: Awful performance of gal gadot
text:
Expanding on the initial statement, my consistent disappointment with Gal Gadot's performances extends beyond this particular film and permeates her overall filmography. Her vocal delivery frequently lacks the necessary inflection and dynamism to truly engage the audience, often presenting as a flat and monotonous drone that hinders the emotional resonance of her lines. This absence of vocal variation makes it challenging to fully invest in her characters and their experiences. Moreover, her portrayal of emotions often feels superficial and unconvincing. Whether the scene calls for joy, sorrow, or anger, the depth and nuance required to create a believable and impactful emotional connection with the viewer seem to be consistently missing. This latest role, unfortunately, has only served to solidify my long-held opinion regarding her limitations as an actress. The nuances and complexities that could have elevated the character were lost, further highlighting a fundamental lack of acting prowess.
Beyond the technical aspects of her performance, there is also a persistent sense of haughty arrogance that emanates from her on-screen persona. This perceived self-importance can be distracting and creates a barrier between the character and the audience, making it difficult to empathize or connect with her motivations. It often feels as though she is presenting rather than embodying the role. Furthermore, her on-screen presence appears to be plagued by an internal conflict, a kind of identity crisis that manifests in performances that are jarringly inconsistent. At times, she seems to overcompensate, resulting in exaggerated and theatrical portrayals that lack subtlety and realism. Conversely, there are moments where she appears underwhelming and detached, failing to command the scene or leave a lasting impression. This constant fluctuation between being over-the-top and surprisingly bland creates a disjointed and ultimately unsatisfying viewing experience. The lack of a grounded and consistent characterization makes it impossible to fully immerse oneself in the narrative. In conclusion, considering her persistent struggles with vocal delivery, emotional depth, a perceived air of arrogance, and inconsistent character portrayals, I remain convinced that Gal Gadot's casting in this and other significant film projects has been a disservice to the potential of those stories and a source of ongoing disappointment for me as a viewer. title: A fun, blocky adventure that captures the spirit of the game
text:

The movie manages to balance humor, heart, and some genuinely impressive visuals, all while staying true to the spirit of the game. The animation style is crisp but still keeps that classic blocky Minecraft aesthetic, which fans will definitely appreciate.
What stood out most was how the film builds an emotional arc from such a simple concept - mining, building, exploring. The characters are relatable, the story has a clear journey, and there are some fun nods to Minecraft lore that long-time players will love (creepers, endermen, the Nether - it's all here).
Is it going to win an Oscar? Probably not. But it's a great ride for fans of all ages, and especially fun if you've spent hours building your own world in Minecraft. A creative and respectful adaptation that celebrates imagination.

Instead of being a kind-hearted princess, she spends most of the movie brooding and delivering stiff dialogue. The Evil Queen, who should be a highlight, is reduced to a generic villain with zero menace. And don't even get me started on the "dwarfs"-sorry, the random group of people that replace them. They're just... there.
The visuals? Somehow both overproduced and lifeless. The forest looks like a screensaver, and the CGI creatures make 2019's Cats look like a masterpiece. The songs? Disney has been on a mission to remake every classic, but this one should've stayed in the vault. If you love Snow White, save yourself the pain and just rewatch the animated version. This one is the fairest of them all... at being completely unnecessary.

author: Movieenjoyer-89P13
title: Absolute Cinema 🥀🥀💔
text:
Ts film is not just a movie. No-ts is an experience, an astral journey, a rite of passage across realms both digital and divine. The Minecraft Movie doesn't merely adapt the beloved game-it transcends it. What begins as a story of survival and creativity soon evolves into an epic saga of identity, purpose, and the quiet beauty of placing a block exactly where it belongs.
From the opening frame, ts film defies the rules of time and space. Its visuals pulse with nostalgic energy and futuristic ambition, its sound design whispers secrets from the far edges of the multiverse. The pacing? Impeccable. The emotional beats? So deep, they echo across dimensions.
And yet, with all its grandeur, ts movie remains grounded in the core values of Minecraft itself: freedom, imagination, and the joy of building something out of nothing. It doesn't need a sprawling ensemble or forced drama-ts knows when to breathe, when to punch you in the feels, and when to let you simply exist in its beautifully blocky world.
There are moments-especially in the final act-where you'll feel your soul lift out of your body, your childhood memories hugging your heart as a single tear rolls down your cheek, whispering:
"Ts... is cinema."
11/10. A masterpiece of block-breaking proportions. Ts movie doesn't just raise the bar-it crafts it from obsidian, enchants it, and sets it at the edge of the universe.

author: DavidR-56
title: Bad, just bad
text: Everything about this movie is so undeniably, atrociously bad. From the casting to the plot to the graphics, everything feels lazy and quickly thrown together. There are many cringe moments that were hard to sit through. The entire thing seems to be made by people who either have only heard about the game, or watched modded YouTubers play for an hour. The movie also includes many things and has items not in the game, meaning they had to make up new things for their bad plot to work, making me wonder if it would have been so hard for them to make a movie actually based on the large amount of canon items always being added to the game. I would not be proud to have my name attached to this movie. I wish i had waited to watch this movie for free because I do not believe it was worth the $15 I spent to watch it in theater. This all being said, there are a couple moments that made me laugh. Unfortunately these were few and far between the cringe lines, poor dialogue, oddly placed songs, and uncomfortably placed "life lessons" which felt like random time fillers which were honestly unnecessary. This movie made me sad as I know how much potential Minecraft has. I have been playing Minecraft since 2013, and the community surrounding it has grown tremendously since I started playing. I know that no one is truly satisfied with this "Minecraft Movie" and I know that I am personally sad to see such little effort and cringe trying to reflect the game that so many of us know and love. This is a cheap money grab because those who made it knew that no matter how terrible the movie, the games fans would pay to watch it and they would still make money. This movie was made as cheaply as possible for max profit, and I feel cheated out of a potentially epic movie that could have been. Overall, this movie is one that you should watch once, for free, and see if you personally like it, but I am confident that for the vast majority of Minecraft players and fans, this movie is a letdown. Also there is no reason for Jack Black to sing any songs in the Minecraft movie.

title: Insanely large Budget for what exactly?
text:
The story is set in a forest, not a bustling city like New York during peak hours-so creating an immersive fairytale world shouldn't have been a monumental task. Yet, despite this, the film fails to deliver even the simple charm of a visually appealing fairy tale. If Pixar had made this movie, the CGI would have been far superior, the protagonist more likable, and the humor more effective.
We all know this classic story, and we all know where it's headed. What we wanted was to lose ourselves in an old German fairy tale, but that proved impossible due to poor CGI, cheap costumes, lackluster acting, and an overall lack of magic. I have to say, René doesn't seem suited for Hollywood-unlike Gal Gadot, who at least brings some star power. If you're considering watching this in theaters, you may want to think twice; no cinema screen can elevate a mediocre production.

author: gavin-thelordofthefu-48-460297
title: A timeless and unforgettable start of a great entertainment industry
text:
Before the beginning of the World War II in the 1940s, an entertainment industry was born and while most of the movies were made in the early 1910s and 1920s, a man named Walt Disney and several of his workers created a company known as the Walt Disney Company, a light-hearted entertainment industry, by releasing their very first animated full length feature, "Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs" based on the Grimm fairy tale of the same name.
It tells the story about Snow White, a girl dressed rags who meets a prince. The queen, after becoming jealous of her beauty which will result in taking the queen's place as ruler of the kingdom, sends his huntsman to take her far into the forest where he can kill her. When he tried to kill her, he apparently lets her go after telling her of the Queen's plan. She runs into a forest, but after making some encounters with some forest friends, they take her to a cottage where she along with the animals clean it up. Little does Snow White know that this cottage belongs to the seven dwarf men, who then find her and decided to make friends with her and let her stay for as long as she likes. Meanwhile, the Queen, having found out the Snow White is still alive, transforms herself into an old hag and makes a poison apple so she can give it to her and will result in sleeping death.
For their first attempt at an animated feature that will lead to their success and create other classics, Disney has done a fantastic job and to me, I remembered watching this as a child and it finally grew out on me which is why I'm giving this a full 100%. The story is very original with an emotional feeling to it and the pacing is really good with some scenes that aren't drag. The characters are extremely likable. Snow White, although the weakest of the other Disney princess, is at least decent, the prince only appears in the beginning and the end, but was OK. The seven dwarfs are so funny. Doc, Happy, Sleepy, Grumpy, Happy, Dopey, and Sneezy are great and the hilarious moments with them are enjoyable to watch, but the only character who steals the show the most is the Queen who is by far a great Disney villain. Her motives are excellent and her old hag form scared the living soul out of me as a child. The voice acting for the characters are what I would like to say "excellent", but the strongest aspects goes to the memorable songs (I'm Wishing, Whistle While You Work, Heigh Ho, The Silly Song, Someday My Prince Will Come) and the beautiful animation I've ever seen in any film out there today.
Overall, Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs will always remain to Disney-fans as one of the most classic films in cinema history before MGM would later do the same thing by making The Wizard of OZ, an adaptation of L. Frank Baum's classic book. This deserves a higher thumbs up from me!

author: bthardamaz
title: (Another) Easter Egg Hunt.
text:
Typically when it comes to movie adaptations of beloved games, it is rather hard to appeal to everyone. There are two different audiences; one being your average person being to see the newest release, then you got those who are knowledgeable of the source, and wish to see it come to the silver screens.
Often times, it can be hard to balance out the two people. These films often times play too hard into references, cameos and nods. Reverence to the source is a vital factor for these films. Showing much needed respect and love for the source is needed to appeal for the very reason you exist - being a faithful adaptation.
However, these can easily clog the creative minds of it's creators, often leading to a movie that has heart, but without soul. Being more concerned with reference points than telling a genuine story that can touch not just the game enthusiasts, but your average person, who may not understand.
Say, if Sonic the Hedgehog (1-3) mastered subtle references; small little things that don't change the trajectory of the story, but still serve as a momentary treat for the fans, then A Minecraft Movie embodies the antithesis of this.
Asides from Black and Momoa's entertaining exuberance, A Minecraft Movie is thoroughly dull in both character and story. Further exacerbating this would be the frequent homages to it's source. This isn't offensive by itself, but the story typically hinges on these artifacts and items from the video game to further the story.
These items in question aren't explained and are simply passed off as crucial plot points because they're useful in the source material. The average filmgoer isn't going to know what these things are, and will be left confused. It actively lets the references control the story. Many instances exist within A Minecraft Movie where the characters need to do something, they use a reference to get it done and then never speak of it again. That is the depth that the film runs on. One that factors the fans, but absolutely no one else.
The film takes no time to elaborate much on our protagonists before being shoved into new world. We only receive faint cliff notes, which aren't enough to get a grasp on their characters to a deep extent. Steve (Jack Black) doesn't work as a convincing survivalist, because everything he ever does relies on Easter Eggs rather than proper tenacity or smarts. And the villain, Malgosha's motivations are hollow, nonsensical and are even dismissed towards the third act. She more so serves as a generic bad guy who sends grunts to do the hard work rather than making an impact herself.
Dismissing the nightmarish animation, (Full animation would've served better) A Minecraft Movie is rather ironic. It's a grand adventure with a witty group of characters, out to stop the big bad from doing bad things. This remarkably, is far from original and is further hurt by the shallow characters, plot and worldbuilding. It is a contradiction of itself. In the vain effort to create a story centered around the power of creativity, the movie is remarkably shallow.
This is disappointing considering that it's message being that being creative and unique isn't inherently bad - it's how you go about it that matters. You can either be Steve and use your smarts to accomplish great things, or become apathetic like Malgosha, and come to despise innovation (Even if in film it's conveyed rather poorly.) This is a great central theme, but A Minecraft Movie is too concerned with the next, fleeting reference to consider it.
No doubt, the enthusiasts will revel with the nods to the game, and it still on its own is an entertaining film, but those who are embarking to find an experience that'll make them think, had better look elsewhere; A Minecraft Movie isn't the creative endeavor they're looking for.

author: nbutcher-69458
title: Everything is sort of awesome?
text:
Here we go with another video game adaption. This movie is one for the fans and the kids. They'll have a good time with this one so I won't rain on their parade. Adults on the other hand - unless they've played the game - are going to be asking themselves what on earth they're witnessing. I think there's going to be a certain section of the community that will find this one a better watch in different states of altered consciousness.
This is a fun movie that wants to be as silly as possible while being completely self-aware. This is going to attract a certain kind of moviegoer that likes an awkward and cringe "so-bad-it's-good" experience. In my viewing, there was a lot of audience participation, shout outs, and things being thrown up at the screen. This could shape up to be the next "The Room" or "Rocky Horror Show" for all I know.
All the same, it's a confused movie trying to jam as many callbacks and fanservice moments into the story when it barely fits into coherency. It has a sluggish start with too much pointless exposition. The jokes are there, but they're mostly in-jokes that the fans will love. Only a scant few good ones will manage to land for the uninitiated.
I take issue with the art direction. It's creepier than the Minecraft video game is, and when the violence happens it's a bit unsettling for very young kids who are more familiar with the game's harmless visuals. If the film stuck to keeping the visual language the same as the video game and maybe used voice actors instead of live acting it wouldn't have been as awkward. Just look at the violence in the LEGO movies for reference. It's funnier and more harmless there because it accurately represents the toy and is not hyper realistic at all.
As for the acting: it's a Jack Black movie so you can expect that he'll be playing as Jack Black instead of ... you know... doing any acting. He pulls in a few stupid songs as he is does in other films. Jason Momoa gets a few puerile laughs trying to play a buffoonish alpha male. The other characters feel tacked on and sadly forgettable. Basically there's no Oscar awards to hand out here in this film.
It's an entertaining film just for its sheer ridiculousness, but it's not a brilliant piece of cinema by a long shot. It's more of a cash grab, but Minecraft fans will love it regardless no matter what the critics say. My five year old thought it was a lot of fun, and judging by the box office and post-credit sequence, a sequel is all but assured.

author: Alexs-263
title: The best movie
text:
I just finished "a minecraft movie" here is my honest review:
I had to sit with this movie after I watched it-it was a masterpiece. What starts off as a light-hearted children's film quickly transforms into something far more impactful. The tonal shift was bold, and it paid off massively.
The first hour lulls you in with nostalgia and innocent fun. But then... the group stumbles upon Steve's villager trading camp, and everything changes. The film leans hard into the horror aspects of Minecraft-and it works. Seeing Steve portrayed as a cold, brutal figure, only allowing villagers to "crush loaf" in order to breed, was disturbing in the best way. It reframes what we've all accepted as "just game mechanics" into something deeply unsettling. That scene hit hard.
From there, the descent into madness continues. The escape to the Redstone Mines, discovering Steve's hidden diamond stash, and then the perfectly timed line:
"No, not that minecart-we take the diamond minecart."
That was genius. A subtle but hilarious nod to DanTDM that longtime fans will absolutely appreciate.
And then... the Piglin sequence. Easily one of the most emotionally jarring parts of the film. Watching them desperately try to please Steve as he throws 64 gold ingots on their heads, only to be discarded once he gets their "Ender peals"-it was heartbreaking. The film gave voice and feeling to NPCs we've always treated as disposable, and it made me genuinely reconsider how I interact with the game.
My only real complaint? They never showed Herobrine. With how far the movie leaned into the mythology and darker tone, it felt like a missed opportunity. That said, maybe they're saving him for the sequel.
Final Verdict: 13/10.
Incredible world-building, smart meta-commentary on how players treat NPCs, and an unforgettable tonal shift. Whether you're a longtime Minecraft fan or just curious, this one deserves a watch-and probably a long sit afterward to process what you just saw.

author: The_Movie_Cat
title: "A fine bunch of washers you lot turned out to be!"
text:
I feel ashamed that I only watched Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs in order so that my hard, cynical heart could launch itself into an anti-Disney rant. The most sentimental of the major cartoon studios, I was determined to ravage this one after seeing isolated, treacly clips.
Yet seen all together I have to admit that I was softened by a talented picture that is genuinely charming. The somewhat dated animation resembles cut outs from a picture book with its pastel hues, and looks and feels more natural than the angular, jerky computerised movement of the modern Disney features. It helps that they also employ someone who can actually sing in the titular role, with an operatic blend to the proceedings. And it would take the coldest of people not to warm to Snow White's genuine innocence. I concede, I did wince a little at the cutesy blue birds, but this is vastly more charming than I had been led to expect.
It's pacy, too: whereas some of the older Disney films tend to drag (I remember catching the aptly named Sleeping Beauty one Sunday afternoon), this one is suitably brisk in its portrayal of events. And while modern cartoons (or "Animated Features" as they pompously like to be known) blow up the role of the "director", this one really has its eye on cinematic technique. Just look at the early wishing well scene, shot from the perspective of the well bottom or the blend of images and dissolves when Snow White's in the forest.
Many of the songs are classics, of course. Whistle While You Work is still something you can find yourself humming or whistling while doing the hoovering, The greatest contention for me though was the seven dwarves, who always struck me as far too self-consciously cutesy and grating to really like. Yet, come on  It's Off To Work We Go is a belter, isn't it?
The actual plot, which is largely sidestepped to make way for the leisurely song sequences, is more than a little macabre. Even when Snow White's heart (her severed heart!) is substituted; it's replaced with a pig's heart... and all for a family audience. I'm not saying this one is morbid, but they deem Snow White (Or Snow, if we may call her that) so "beautiful, even in death" that they refuse to bury her and place her in a transparent coffin. In a parallel universe somewhere there's an offshoot of this movie where the Prince arrives too late and her rapidly decaying corpse turns into a flesh-eating zombie. Maybe they should do that as one of their special straight-to-video sequels  after all, they're grave robberies, aren't they?
It's a slightly strange plot, too, with Snow White spending the duration being plotted against by a bitter old Queen. And people say Elton John didn't get involved with Disney until The Lion King. Yet in order to elicit Snow White's trust she transforms herself into a scary-looking old hag? Why not just stay in her own image? And if she can transform her appearance like that, then why not use the same magic to make herself the sought-after "fairest of them all"? Yet I guess if she didn't then we wouldn't have a story, and the apple ofference does have some religious connotations. This is a one-note plot, though, and subtext isn't the order of the day. Rather, it's the colour and flavouring of the piece that are there to be enjoyed, not the somewhat redundant narrative. And while, after the initial thrust, the film does lose momentum slightly, enjoy it I did, a delightful and wonderfully made cartoon. Yes, you can read into the white = good/black evil assertions, but for me I'd rather marvel at the songs and images, or make cheap jokes about MOR pianists.
Just two minor points: why are they called "Dwarfs" and not Dwarves in the film's title? And seven dwarves working in a mine? Is that an example of positive discrimination?

author: jboothmillard
title: Mickey 17
text: Parasite made history at the Academy Awards, winning Best Picture, Best International Feature Film, and Best Director for Bong Joon Ho (Memories of Murder, The Host, Snowpiercer); I was most excited to see his next movie, only his third English language film. Basically, in the year 2054, Mickey Barnes (Robert Pattinson) and his friend Timo (Steven Yeun) have financial troubles after a failed business venture. Unable to repay a murderous loan shark, they fled and signed up as crew for a spaceship that leaves Earth to colonise the planet Niflheim. While Timo becomes a shuttle pilot, Mickey becomes "Expendable", a disposable crew member. Cloning technology is banned on Earth, so Mickey is selected for dangerous tasks on the distant planet, and if he dies, his body can be regenerated, and his recent memories restored. During the four-year voyage to the ice planet, Mickey forms a romantic relationship with security agent Nasha (Naomi Ackie). With Mickey carrying out several missions and being cloned several times, the spaceship's scientists develop a vaccine against Niflheim's pathogens. On his seventeenth iteration, Mickey is tasked to capture Niflheim's tardigrade-like lifeform for analysis; the alien creatures are nicknamed "creepers". Mickey 17 falls into a narrow opening in the ice, and Timo cannot reach him. Timo leaves him for dead, assuming he will not make it out alive. Mickey 17 sees several creepers approaching and assumes they are about to devour him, but he is surprised when they collectively carry him out to the surface. Mickey 17 returns to the spaceship and is shocked to meet the newly generated Mickey 18. Politician Kenneth Marshall (Mark Ruffalo), leader of the expedition, has vowed to kill any "Multiples" (simultaneously living clones). Mickey 18, who is more aggressive, tries to kill Mickey 17, who resists, suggesting that they could live and secretly rotate duties, meals, and deaths. Mickey 18 then tries to kill Timo but is interrupted and leaves with Nasha. Mickey 17 spends the evening at dinner with Marshall, his wife Ylfa (Toni Collette), and security agent Kai Katz (Anamaria Vartolomei), to celebrate the capture of the creeper. Mickey 17 suffers severe pain after being served experimental meat and being treated with experimental painkillers. Kai intervenes to stop Marshall from executing Mickey 17, and he flees when Kai tries to woo him. Mickey 17 returns to his room, where Nasha is with Mickey 18 having learnt of them both, but she has accepted the situation. Kai discovers the Mickeys and goes to report them, but Nasha stops him. When Mickey 17 tells Mickey 18 what happened at dinner, an enraged Mickey 18 decides to kill Marshall at a public ceremony commemorating a piece of Niflheim rock. Then the rock cracks open and chaos ensues when two baby creepers emerge from it. Mickey 17 arrives and captures one baby creeper, named Zoco, while the other baby creeper, named Luko, jumps onto Marshall and is killed by Kai and other security agents. Nasha stops Mickey 18 from killing Marshall, who discovers the Multiples. Mickey 17, Mickey 18 and Nasha are arrested. Outside the ship, a swarm of creepers arrive, calling out to Zoco. In the brig, Mickey 17 describes being rescued by the creepers and Nasha realises they are sentient. Timo tries to kill Mickey 17 to satisfy the loan shark, but he is overpowered by Nasha and Mickey 18. The Mickeys and Nasha are brought to Marshall, who wants to exterminate the creepers. Marshall destroys Mickey's stored memories and DNA, meaning he cannot be cloned again, while Nasha saves Zoco from being executed by Ylfa. Marshall's assistant Preston (Daniel Henshall) persuades Marshall to task the Mickeys to compete in collecting creeper tails, which Ylfa wants to use to make an edible sauce, and the winner will be allowed to live. The Mickeys are forced to comply as they are fitted with remote-detonated bomb vests. When the Mickeys are sent out, they find the creepers' leader and are peaceful with it. Marshall watches this and goes outside himself with a security team, intending to personally kill the creepers. Using a translation device, Mickey 17 communicates with the creepers' leader, informing it of Marshall's plan. The creepers' leader threatens to kill all humans unless Zoco is returned alive. Mickey 17 communicates to Nasha on camera mentioning a sexual position she recognises. She realises he is saying that they need to free Zoco. Nasha takes Ylfa hostage to ensure Zoco's release. Ylfa is released and tries to kill Zoco, but Nasha again saves him. The security agents arrest Ylfa. Zoco is returned by Nasha to the creepers' leader, while Mickey 18 attacks Marshall. Mickey 18 detonates the bomb planted on his vest, killing himself and Marshall to fulfil the creepers' leader's demand. In the aftermath, Ylfa is traumatised by her husband's death and tries to clone him but is taken to a psychiatric ward and later commits suicide. Preston and other Marshall collaborators are imprisoned. An associate of the loan shark tries to kill Timo, but Timo manages to kill him. Nasha goes on to be elected as a colony political leader. She officiates a ground-breaking ceremony on Niflheim, where Mickey 17 (now "Mickey Barnes") detonates the cloning device, ending the Expendable program. Also starring Patsy Ferran as Dorothy, Cameron Britton as Arkady, Steve Park as Zeke, Holliday Grainger (former child star of Roger and the Rottentrolls) as Red Hair, Angus Imrie (Celia's son) as Agent Charlie, Tim Key as the Pigeon Man, and This Is England's Thomas Turgoose as the Bazooka Soldier. Pattinson gives good performances as the leading characters with changing personalities, I found Ruffalo annoying as the big-toothed Trump-esque megalomaniac, Collette is just as annoying as his wife, and Ackie was okay. The cloning "re-printing" plot was interesting enough, and it does have terrific special effects to create the alien creatures and all other extra-terrestrial stuff. Unfortunately, it was not the film I expected or had hoped for, the overall vibe was perhaps too absurd, I wanted it to be darker, funnier, and more exciting, I found it rather dull, a disappointing but alright science-fiction black comedy. Worth watching!

author: ShannonK-46
title: Lazy, Cash-Grabbing and Tiresome
text:
I did not have high hopes whatsoever before going into this film, but I hoped that maybe I was just being cynical, as I usually am. A Minecraft Movie, however, managed to disappoint even my exceedingly low expectations. It is laced with boring, tired tropes and honestly disrespects a source material that I have loved since I was a child. I tried to have fun, I really really did! I even laughed at some parts (hence the 2 stars)! However, for a movie that asks the audience to be creative and to chase their wildest dreams, it is clear that this film follows the typical Hollywood archetypes to a T; there is no uniqueness, creativity or understanding of the game or the audience in this film.
Now I hear what you might be thinking: "this is a movie about Minecraft, a game for kids, you can't really have been expecting some ground breaking high art cinema?" I did not! I wanted it to be FUN. But I found myself, 45 minutes into the film, desperately wanting to leave. Minecraft is a game that broke barriers, it brought life to a new genre of video game! And for it's name to be attached to a movie script that could honestly be copy pasted onto any other franchise is disappointing. I thought the characters were lacking depth and dull, I thought some of the humour was inane and pointless, and I thought the point of the movie was entirely hypocritical, to make a long story short.
I cannot recommend this film any less, on a moral basis. It's clear that this film suffered at the hands of Hollywood executives just wanting a quick and easy cash grab. I do think the actors did the best with the script they had, and it's clear that they had a lot of fun on set, but it does not save the film in the slightest. Maybe I'm just getting tired and grumpy at 20 years old, who knows. Maybe it just wasn't made for the type of person I am! The story, though simple, revolves around a group of characters racing to save the Minecraft world from an impending disaster. While it doesn't delve too deeply into character development, the film succeeds in creating an engaging and fun journey, filled with action, humor, and moments of surprise. Fans will appreciate how the movie incorporates game elements, such as crafting tools and using redstone, which adds a layer of authenticity to the narrative.
The voice acting is solid, with a cast that brings the characters to life despite the minimalist designs. The pacing is generally well-balanced, though some parts could have used more emotional depth, especially for the protagonist, Steve, who feels a bit one-dimensional.
Overall, the Minecraft movie is a faithful and entertaining adaptation that will delight fans of the game. It may not be a groundbreaking cinematic masterpiece, but it's a fun, action-packed ride through the beloved Minecraft universe that will leave viewers excited for more.

author: imdbfan-1083819984
title: Sucks
text:
This movie sucks. Walt Disney's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs may be a landmark in animation history, but that doesn't mean it holds up today. For a film often praised as a timeless classic, it feels more like a relic of outdated storytelling, weak character development, and over-simplicity.
The pacing of the film is also an issue. While it's only about 80 minutes long, it drags in parts, particularly with the excessive filler of the dwarfs' antics. Yes, they're cute, but their slapstick humor quickly becomes repetitive. Grumpy is the only one with even a semblance of personality, while the rest are essentially walking gags.
The Evil Queen, while visually striking, has one of the most nonsensical villain plans in Disney history. Instead of just killing Snow White outright, she goes through an elaborate scheme involving a poisoned apple that can easily be undone by "true love's kiss." Not exactly a foolproof strategy.

author: Abcsa_
title: A great set-up for an ultimately dissapointing experience
text:
Bong Joon Ho's Mickey 17 seemed like the perfect movie to watch in theaters. It's an original movie, from a great writer which had an interesting concept and looked like great fun! Well, all of that is only present in the first section of the movie...
The story follows Mickey Barnes, a person trying to flee earth by signing up to be an expendable, having to die over and over again for the benefit of researchers. Hovewer, things get complicated when he survives an alien encounter he was expected to die in. This results in the production of a new Mickey, which generates a wide range of new problems for the 2 simultaneously living clones.
The way this entire storyline is introduced and set up in the first half of the movie really grabs the viewers attention. Being an expendable whose entire job is to die is a uniquely interesting concept. Watching it unfold and getting to know the character is engaging and overall just excellent.
But things quickly start crumbling when Mickey 18 is introduced. It seems like the writer just did not know what to do afterwards. The cloning storyline is entirely thrown away and instead we get pointless side-stories that are just not even remotely interesting. It seems like the movie tries to randomly squeeze in so many things at once, when in truth, none of them should be in the movie. And the actually interesting concepts and themes are just left in the bin. Some things are never even explained, like why different mickeys have such drastically different personalities. It's not what you'd expect after having such a strong base to build on. The rest of the film just ultimately becomes a drag, with one generic scene after another.
The visuals are okay... it's not a beautiful looking movie by any means and does not set any new standards. The acting in this movie is just very off-putting. On one hand you have Robert Pattinson, playing not one, but two different characters. He gives it his all and gives an incredible performance. However, his top tier acting just highlights the contrast between him and his co-stars. No one even came close to his skills in this movie, which made all the other actors feel shallow and soulless. I believe Mark Ruffalo was especially terrible in this film. Of course his character wasn't suppossed to be taken seriously, but he really overacted this one, which just made him aggrivating and annoying to watch. The dialogue doesn't help either. It is incredibly cheesy and on the nose, and the actors' line deliveries just make it painful to watch at times.
Overall, Mickey 17 is not the worst movie I've ever seen, and not a bad movie either. It's just a dissapointingly mid feature thaz could've been way better, especially from someone like Bong Joon Ho.

The supporting characters, intended for comic relief, are grating and one-dimensional. The antagonist's motivations are cartoonish and lack any real depth. The whole thing feels like a morality play hammered over your head with a sledgehammer. It's a classic, yes, but a classic that has not aged well. There are far better animated films out there, with more compelling characters, engaging stories, and less reliance on outdated tropes. This fairy tale is a relic, not a masterpiece.

title: A Soulless Retelling of a Timeless Classic
text:
I was disappointed by the 2025 live-action remake of Snow White. As a fan of the original animated classic, I found this adaptation lacking in charm and magic.

Underwhelming Characters and Storyline

Snow White, played by Rachel Zegler, felt more like a cynical and self-righteous protagonist than the kind and hopeful heroine I remembered. The Seven Dwarfs were underutilized, and their comedic relief fell flat.

Visually Unimpressive

The film's reliance on CGI resulted in dull, uninviting environments. The color palette was muted, and the special effects lacked the wonder and enchantment of the original.

Predictable Pacing and Heavy-Handed Themes

The storyline was predictable, with long stretches of exposition and unnecessary subplots. The themes of beauty, kindness, and courage were handled heavy-handedly, feeling forced and overly simplistic.

Overall Disappointment

Unfortunately, this remake failed to capture the essence of the beloved classic. With underwhelming characters, a predictable storyline, and lackluster visuals, I couldn't recommend this film to fans of the original.

author: MrPaull0324
title: It's definitely worth it if you're a fan
text:
I've loved Minecraft since it was first released, so I had to check this one out. While I wouldn't call it a masterpiece, it was still definitely worth a watch.
First of all, the visuals are beautiful and fully capture the blocky aesthetics and atmosphere of the Minecraft world with the sheer number of landscapes, items, animals, and buildings you see in the game. You even see Steve (Jack Black) building with dirt and Natalie (Emma Myers) forging a diamond sword on a crafting table. All of it brought back so many fun memories for me, and it almost feels like I was watching footage of gameplay, so I'm grateful for the nostalgia and faithfulness to the source material and it's obvious the production crew did their homework on the franchise and knew what they were doing.
The monsters, like zombies and skeletons, are much scarier looking but that's to be expected and is a welcome feature for me. Unfortunately, this also applies to the villagers, who look far creepier and uncannier than their game counterparts. Nevertheless, any Minecraft player will love seeing the game come to life on the big screen.
The acting is a mixed bag. On the one hand, Jack Black and Jason Momoa are having a blast and they're loads of fun to watch. With his energy and charisma, I think Black was the film's biggest highlight and once more proves he has a gift for video game films, especially after nailing it as Bowser in the Super Mario Bros. Movie. But the rest of the characters felt mediocre and forgettable to me and weren't entirely flesh out.
The fight scenes were fun to watch, but the generic story felt fairly uninspired: a ragtag group of people being transported to another world and now must now defeat the villain, Malgosha, before returning home. It's been done before. And I feel like it shared too much in common with the plot from Jake Kasdans Jumanji series.
In the end, this was nothing too new or special as far as video game films go, but I wasn't expecting it to be anyway. It's still a fun, silly movie and a must watch for fans of the game.

title: Garbage
text:
If you thought Hollywood had already hit rock bottom, think again - the new "Snow White" (2025) manages to dig even deeper. This isn't just a bad movie; it's a masterclass in how to ruin a classic, trample on its legacy, and insult audiences who just wanted a good story.
Let's start with the plot. The original fairy tale? Forget it. The magic? Completely erased. Instead, we get a painfully predictable and dull script that desperately tries to be "modern" but ends up feeling like a poorly written fanfiction. The moral messaging is so heavy-handed that even kids will roll their eyes.
The acting? Absolutely atrocious. The lead actress looks like she was forced into the role-zero emotion, zero charisma, zero effort to actually embody the character. The supporting cast? Either erased or replaced with such bland personalities that you'll forget they existed the moment you leave the theater.
Visuals and CGI? It's as if the budget was spent on anything but decent animation. The CGI is so awful it feels like a relic from the early 2000s. Even the natural environments look artificial, and the supposed "magic" is completely lifeless.
And finally, the worst part - the film's tone. Instead of a charming, whimsical fairy tale, we get a pretentious, preachy lecture that sucks the joy out of every scene. It's like sitting through a two-hour sermon instead of watching an actual story unfold. The heart and soul of the original have been completely lost.
Final verdict: If you have two hours to spare, do something more productive-like watching paint dry. That would be far more entertaining than this soulless, uninspired, and downright terrible film.

author: NoMoviesAreBad
title: The Minecraft Movie is the New Rocky Horror Picture Show
text:
While most people will focus on the audience interaction, I want to make that the smallest part of this review. I will say that I loved the crowd participation, and I was proudly one of the ones participating. It added to the experience in more ways than I can describe. And if you found it annoying, you should have waited for the movie to hit streaming, because this theatrical showing wasn't made for you. Going to the movies is about more than just watching a film-it's about the adventure the silver screen invites us into. What Rocky Horror did for cinema fifty years ago, I hope The Minecraft Movie does for the next fifty. I hope this becomes a yearly tradition, returning to theaters again and again, bringing the experience with it.
Now, onto the actual movie.
Yes, it's a constant lore info dump. But somehow, it keeps its charm. That might be my familiarity with the franchise, but even the references I didn't understand still felt important. The film has a way of inviting you in, regardless of how much you already know.
In some ways, it reminded me of a goofy Jumanji. Well-goofier. Both films star Jack Black, both take place inside a game world, both feature a big Samoan guy and a nerdy kid with no friends. But that's really where the comparison ends. While the similarities might seem blatant, and at times feel like intentional mirroring, these films couldn't be more different in tone. Comparing them too closely sells both short.
The Minecraft Movie refuses to take itself seriously-and because of that, it shouldn't be judged seriously either. The script is riddled with charm and, in its own way, quite brilliantly written. It does stumble a bit when it reaches for emotional depth, and honestly, I don't think it needed to go there at all. But that doesn't take anything away from the experience. It's part of the chaos, and the chaos is the point.
PG Jack Black is cinema gold. It feels like we followed his School of Rock character into a portal and landed here. At times, it played like a long-lost Tenacious D sketch-only this time, the raciness is replaced by pure joy. He takes the role seriously in the best way. He doesn't fully believe himself, but he believes in the fun, and that's even better.
And then there's Momoa.
Jason Momoa is one of the most charismatic comedic actors of our generation, and it's time we start saying that more often. Every time he's on screen, he commands attention. Every line is timed with precision, and he knows exactly what kind of movie he's in. He's not playing the game-he's hosting it.
That's why, unfortunately, some of the rest of the cast feels a little flat by comparison. Sebastian Hansen's portrayal of Henry (or Hank, as Garrett calls him) delivers the film's only moment of genuine emotional resonance, and he absolutely nails it. In a world where every character is cranked to eleven, delivering a sincere emotional beat without breaking the tone deserves an award of its own.
The same can't quite be said for Natalie and Dawn-not because Emma Myers or Danielle Brooks gave poor performances, but because their roles didn't serve much purpose in the larger story. I'd argue that an alternate cut without their scenes might actually make the film stronger, not as a criticism of them, but of how grounded their characters were in a world that thrives on absurdity. Hess's direction leaned realistic in spots where it didn't need to, though that likely came from studio notes more than creative impulse. Judging by Hess's previous work, realism isn't his priority, and that's okay.
Still, there's joy to be found in every performance. From the Pauly Shore-esque pig to the eternally-horny Jennifer Coolidge (a cinematic trope that remains hilariously relevant), every character adds texture to this world. Even the villain, with a backstory that reads like a Mad Lib, somehow works. She's despicable, with zero redeeming qualities-and honestly, it's refreshing to have a villain that just is.
Visually, the CG is near perfect. The Minecraft aesthetic was faithfully translated into something hyperreal without losing its blocky soul-the textures work. The world feels right. And the characters never seem out of place in it.
What stayed with me most, though, was the commentary. The idea that it's easier to destroy than to create-beautiful. That is the message. And the film doesn't whisper it. It looks critics dead in the eye and says it loud. It's punk. It's proud. And we need more of that.
As I write this, I've seen that a sequel is already confirmed. Will it strike the same chord? Probably not. But I hope it does. While this movie was far from perfect, it did exactly what it set out to do. And it's lighting up the box office every single day.
Dislike it all you want. The Minecraft Movie has carved its place into Hollywood history-and it belongs there.

author: cruelworldfilms
title: WTF?!
text:
The Good: It's a riot!
The Bad: It's a riot!
The Verdict: WTF did I just watch? "A Minecraft Movie" is an awesome throwback to days before the early 2000s, before a time where, what I call, "The Jason Bourne/Batman Begins Effect" took hold of movies and everything was a political and/or psychological deconstruction of modern storytelling. To put it simply, this movie just DGAF. It's only agenda is it doesn't take itself seriously, despite a subtle commentary on growing up and the death of creativity in a digitally-evolving world. Easily the best video-game based movie compared to the rest of recent times (I'm judging you-- "Mortal Kombat" (2021), "Borderlands" (2024), "Sonic The Hedgehog" (2020) (a threequel already? Really?! The 1st wasn't even that good and only did well as a protest against the criminally underrated "Birds of Prey (and The Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn" (2020), but I digress). Anyway, this latest entry from Jared Hess ("Napoleon Dynamite" (2004), "Nacho Libre" (2006)) should be awful, awful, a thousand times AWFUL... but it isn't! It's just a hella fun, dumb, crazy, trippy romp through 16-bit imagination and it works! The cast are spot on, the plot is minimal, and the tone is consistent. If I had to find a flaw, it'd be the 3rd act which dragged on a wee bit, but that's a minor criticism. A perfect movie to kick start the weekend and to nurse that hangover afterwards. It's a mash-up of "Jumanji: Welcome To The Jungle" (2017), "Barbie" (2023), "Kangaroo Jack" (2003) and your favourite stoner/bromance comedy. Moreover, like the rise in modern retro-gaming-- next-gen graphics can't beat good, old-fashioned gameplay. I had a blast!
