author: JOSE_17
title: Visually engaging, but emotionally shallow."
text:
Mickey 17 is a film that grabs your attention visually from the start - the cinematography is undeniably beautiful, and there are moments where the visual storytelling almost says more than the dialogue. The score is serviceable, creating the right atmosphere without standing out too much, and Robert Pattinson delivers a strong solo performance, often anchoring the narrative amid a somewhat empty ensemble.
But here's the letdown: the film never quite lives up to the potential of its concept. With such a thought-provoking premise, you'd expect something deeper - a film that challenges ideas about identity, purpose, or even the ethics of immortality. Instead, Mickey 17 stays at surface level, offering glimpses of bigger themes without ever diving into them.
It's not that it's a bad movie - it's well-made, competently acted, and stylistically sharp. It just doesn't leave a lasting impact. It feels like a film you watch once, nod at appreciatively, and then forget about the next day. Definitely not something I'd recommend to someone looking for a sci-fi with emotional or philosophical weight.
Watch it for the aesthetics, maybe for Pattinson, but don't expect it to change your life - or even your weekend.

author: Aemto7
title: Absolute cinema
text:
Bong Joon Ho has done it again. Mickey 17 isn't just another sci-fi flick-it's a philosophical punch to the gut disguised as a dark comedy set on an icy, dying world. I'm giving it a solid 10/10 because it's rare to find a movie this bold, this weird, and this emotionally resonant, all at the same time.

At the center of it all is Robert Pattinson, playing multiple versions of Mickey Barnes-a man who's literally cloned over and over to die for the sake of his colony's survival. Pattinson crushes it. Each clone has its own subtle quirks, fears, and rebellions, and he pulls them off effortlessly. It's like watching someone act opposite himself and still have chemistry.

The genius of Mickey 17 is how Bong blends bleak existential themes with biting humor and a strangely warm undercurrent. You laugh at the absurdity, then realize you're being dragged into deep questions about identity, autonomy, and the value of a single life. The sci-fi worldbuilding is top-tier, but it never overshadows the emotional core.

The visuals? Gorgeous and desolate. The pacing? Tight. The satire? Sharp as ever. Bong uses the backdrop of a failing space colony to echo real-world systems-corporate greed, worker exploitation, environmental collapse-but he never sacrifices story for message.

I left the theater thinking, "That was insane... and kinda beautiful."

author: hydralien
title: Somehow less than the sum of its parts
text:
The parts that comprise the movie are quite good - the sci-fi tech and setup, the alien planet with decently unusual life, the general idea of expendable re-printed test subjects (however put on the back-burner way too soon), the ignorant "leader" of the expedition. Even the plot, however uneven and inconsistent it is at times.
But for various reasons, all the parts do not combine into a wholesome movie, or not entirely.
I'm not sure I can pinpoint any specific problem, as for me it was several: main character's motivation, behaviour and some sudden personality changes were not explained much (or sometimes at all); inconsistencies in the logic for the re-printing process; disjointed or too self-centered performances of some characters, and a noticeable number of dubious character decisions.
It's not a bad movie - it's well made, it has great visuals, great actors, it satirises relevant subjects and raises deep questions under a satirical facade. But unfortunately, it's put together too unevenly to call it great.

author: kuarinofu
title: Great score
text:
I haven't read the source material, so I'll judge the film solely on its own merits. I also won't compare it to or rate it based on the director's previous work.
This film was horrible. It's marketed as a dark comedy, but all the comedy is substituted with cringe-worthy dialogue and acting. It's a parody supposedly satirizing reality, yet reality is far more extreme compared to how tame the film presents itself.
While it offers an original story, it's completely directionless, merely wandering from scene to scene. Even if you accept everything in the film as satirical sci-fi, there are still no interesting characters and no emotional attachment whatsoever.
The messages they attempt to convey are so childish and barebones that they actually feel offensive to a thoughtful mind.
Overall, the film was a visionless, unfocused, cringeworthy mess with obvious references but without a single intellectual or humorous moment.
There's no reason to look for plot holes since there is no comprehensible plot, structure, or rules; the scenes simply follow each other and ultimately lead nowhere.
I was hopeful that this film would offer something interesting since I admire some of the director's previous work (not specifically Parasite), so I was quite disappointed.
Nevertheless, I forced myself to finish it to be able to comment on the complete picture.
It wasn't witty or smart, not truly satirical, not a comedy in general-just a boring story with tedious scenes of overacting and unlikable characters.
The score was cool; that's the only positive aspect this film deserves.

author: MrSelfPaid
title: Wah?
text:
This has to be one of the most disappointing films I've seen from a great director in quite some time. If someone had told me that the same mind behind 'Parasite' was responsible for this movie, I would have genuinely questioned their sanity. It's baffling how a filmmaker known for such a masterful blend of tone, tension, and social commentary could have crafted something so directionless and incoherent.
The film suffers from a profound identity crisis. It doesn't seem to know what genre it belongs to or what story it's trying to tell. One moment it flirts with satire, the next it leans into melodrama, only to abruptly shift into surreal absurdity - and not in a way that feels intentional or earned. There's no cohesive tone, no emotional through-line, and certainly no satisfying payoff.
It feels like the work of someone who's trying too hard to be profound while forgetting the basics of storytelling. The characters are thinly drawn, the dialogue borders on self-parody, and the pacing is a slog. Overall, it's a confused mess that lacks the brilliance and focus we've come to expect from a director of this caliber.

author: Thepilotscut
title: When your girlfriend's in love with 18 versions of you - _MattRatedIt_ confusingly loyal.
text:
Mickey 17 - Pilot's Cut (Spoiler Dive)

Let's get one thing straight-Mickey 17 is the most submissive protagonist I've seen in a while. Like, you could shoot this man and he'd probably say, "Thanks for noticing me." And honestly? That kinda makes him endearing.

But here's where it gets wild: Was Mickey 17 still Mickey Barnes?

We see two Mickeys at once, and they're so different in personality. Makes you wonder-are these clones actually the same person, or just recycled memories stuffed into slightly evolved consciousnesses? If they start thinking differently, are they even the same dude anymore?

Then there's that scene-you know the one. The threesome-but-not-really. Nasha, Mickey, and... Mickey. At first, I was like, "Girl, what are you doing?" Felt like cheating on one clone with the other. But when you zoom out, she didn't choose this situation-she lived and loved with every version from 1 to 18. That's a lot of Mickey. So maybe it wasn't betrayal-it was just her being loyal to every piece of the same man?

Also shoutout to Mickey 18-that guy was a badass. Had that edge Mickey 17 lacked.

But now the real question... Did Mickey still have that pimple on his ass?

We'll never know. And maybe that's the most haunting mystery of the film.

author: Maha_MZ
title: thought-provoking sci-fi Film
text:
*Mickey 17* is very beautiful and interesting sci-fi movie. The story is unique and makes you think a lot about life and who we are. The movie is about Mickey Barnes (Robert Pattinson), who is an "expendable." His job is very dangerous, and every time he dies, he comes back in a new body, but with all his memories. It makes you wonder what is really important about being yourself.
Robert Pattinson acts very good, and you can feel how Mickey struggles inside himself. Other actors, like Steven Yeun and Naomi Ackie, also make the story feel alive. The director, Bong Joon Ho, mixes sad moments and funny parts in a very smart way.
The movie production and visual effects are amazing, especially the frozen alien planet. However, I feel like the story does not go deep enough into what happens to Mickey because he keeps dying and coming back. I wish it showed more about his feelings and how this changes him as a person.
Even with this, *Mickey 17* is a great movie that makes you think and enjoy. If you like Bong Joon Ho's movies, you will enjoy it, and if you are new to his work, you will be surprised by how original it is.

author: kindastolen
title: Taking the Mickey
text:
Sci-fi is a great genre because you can do so much with it, so how this film managed to do nothing with it's central premise except turn it into the most obvious satire since Don't Look Up is equally baffling and impressive.

Robert Pattinson is, as usual, great as Mickey 17 and Mickey 18, playing off both personalities quite well, but it takes an hour for us to reach the point where there are two Mickeys and then the plot does essentially nothing with them.

In contrast to Pattinson, Mark Ruffalo plays a character that is so obviously Trump, with his mannerisms and accent impersonation, that his scenes made me physically cringe. It's satire for people who want to feel smart that they understood it when it's staring everyone else in the face.

By the time the script had Ruffalo and his room of cronies making very obvious Nazi salutes (in the style of Elon Musk, despite the movie obviously being filmed before that), all pretense that the film might be a complex and biting satire are lost. Talking of losing two elections in a row didn't pay off here Bong, although a later failed assassination attempt on Trump, sorry Ruffalo, was some incredible foresight.

Political satire fails completely when it's cutting this close to the bone. It will be loudly cheered by some who are fanatically for the concept but for others it's eyeroll worthy. In particular the end speech where the non-white character swearily shouts down Ruffalo is a summation of everything wrong with the movie. Overt and full of itself, assuming no viewer is able to figure things out for themselves and so bludgeoning them with it to get them to understand.

Mickey 17 is an interesting concept totally wasted by Joon Ho getting carried away with himself. Perhaps stick to the satires of Korean culture in future because this was too superficial.

5/10.

author: mrfreddyfilm
title: Still can't stop to think , how it feels To die ? 🤔
text:
I had pretty high expectations going in, mostly because of the director's reputation. While the film didn't completely blow me away, it was still a solid, one-time watch with a lot of interesting elements.

The concept of testing and replicating humans is both fascinating and a little terrifying - especially since it doesn't feel all that far from where we're heading in real life. The execution of that idea was engaging, and I loved how it played with questions of identity and consciousness.

Robert and Mark Ruffalo gave standout performances - grounded, emotional, and believable. They really helped carry the film and make even the more far-fetched moments feel real.

However, the ending was a bit too predictable. That whole "aliens and humans trying to colonize or outsmart each other" thing feels overdone - I've seen that theme rehashed in so many sci-fi movies already. It didn't really offer a fresh take.

Still, I genuinely enjoyed the ride. The film had great pacing, solid tension, and moments of humor and surprise that kept me interested. Even if I saw the twist coming, I was never bored.

And honestly... I'm still stuck on that last thought: what does it actually feel like - to die? 🤔

author: cjonesas
title: [7.5] We are the aliens
text:
'Mickey' started great with an innovative premise, ahead of its time sci-fi, rosy-gray humor and dark comedy. It was fun up until the mamma crawler didn't eat Mickey the 17th and we started seeing the real aliens clown Kenneth Marshall and his mumbo blood-thirsty wife Ylfa.

From then on, it delved into absurd circus, lots of heart-warming scenes and messages and the sci-fi version of it gradually turned to soft jelly.

About 60 minutes into the runtime, I was already snoozing and so struggling to keep my eyes open, thankfully lots of tantrum cringed my ears and I dutifully went on but not with the same interest and excitement.

It's like the movie is scripted by two teams of writers, the first hour is the best and more interesting one with lots of deep funny sci-fi, whereas the second half is like a 'Scary Movie' parody of the same film.

I enjoyed both halves, though they are like a "9" and "6" uneven blend. The problem is the movie leaned too much toward humanity, gentleness and selflessness by the end, finishing on a rather dull note, at least for me.

'Mickey 17' is like a yummy frozen ice cream badly thawing into an unusable syrupy liquid. At over two hours, it's a slight miss unless they wickedly plan to make a sequel.

author: hestia-30771
title: It's weird, it's bold, it's totally Bong.
text:
Mickey 17 is unmistakably Bong Joon Ho-dystopian, thematically layered, and carried by an offbeat hero. It's not trying to be Parasite 2, and thankfully so. That film was a unique milestone in his career, while this one follows a different path.
You can feel Bong's signature in every frame: the world-building, the philosophical undertones, and the subtle but clear social commentary. It's a film that speaks through its strangeness and silence more than exposition.
The performances stood out-Robert Pattinson was great, but Naomi Ackie's performance really surprised me. Ruffalo and Yeun are, as always, solid.
The premise isn't groundbreaking, but the execution is what makes it work. The only real flaw? Marketing. In the U. S., where hype drives visibility, this film was nearly invisible. It deserved more attention.
It's not for everyone, but for fans of Bong's unique worldview and storytelling style, it's absolutely worth the watch.

author: andolini-80524
title: Shockingly good
text:
I watched this movie... and then I watched it again-which should tell you everything you need to know. I absolutely loved this film. From start to finish, it had me locked in. The pacing, the chemistry between the characters, the balance between comedy and storytelling-it was all there.
The humor landed exactly where it needed to. It wasn't forced or over the top; it was that rare kind of comedy where the timing feels natural, almost effortless, like the actors were just having fun and we got to witness it. Every joke hit at the right moment, and even the subtle stuff made me laugh on the second watch when I caught what I missed the first time.
But let me be real here-Robert absolutely made this movie what it is. His performance is magnetic. He walks that fine line between being the heart of the film and the one quietly stealing every scene. The way he delivers lines, his expressions, the timing of every gesture-it's like the role was made for him. He brings so much personality and nuance without ever trying too hard, and that's what makes it feel real. Not just acting-presence.
This is one of those movies I'll be telling people about, the kind I'll rewatch when I need something that just feels good to put on. The writing was tight, the direction was sharp, and every element felt intentional. The whole team deserves credit, but Robert? He deserves applause. He's the glue that held this story together.
In a world full of movies that overdo it or miss the mark, this one stands out for all the right reasons. If you haven't seen it-watch it. And if you already have? Watch it again. It's even better the second time around.

author: SoumikBanerjee1996
title: Not upto Bong Joon-ho standards!
text:
Bong Joon-ho stands out as a filmmaker who consistently weaves profound themes and messages into his narratives, and "Mickey 17" is no exception to this trend.
Building on his previous critiques of unethical scientific practices and societal class disparities in "Okja" and "Parasite," respectively, Bong now delves into the harsher aspects of corporate culture.
He explores the grim realities of employee exploitation and the ruthless tactics employed to fulfill selfish ambitions, valiantly shedding light on darker facets of modern corporate dominance.
The film also touches (albeit slightly) on themes of supremacy and radicalism, portraying individuals who consider themselves 'pure' while viewing others as expendables, all delivered with Joon-ho's signature blend of dark humor and thrill.
However, it is important to note that this film does not quite reach the heights one might expect from a director of his caliber, as compared to the impactful stories he has previously told and the lasting impressions he has made all over the years, this work feels somewhat distant from his true artistic brilliance.
Even the science fiction elements, featuring an alien world and its peculiar inhabitants, while intriguing, come across as underdeveloped and lacking completeness. While not a dreadful work by any means, it certainly exhibits flaws that warranted further attention and refinement.

author: Hakihiko
title: A Bold Concept With Uneven Execution
text:
"Mickey 17" offers a fresh and intriguing sci-fi premise that hooks you early on. With Bong Joon-ho at the helm, expectations are naturally high-and while the film delivers on style, thought-provoking themes, and ambition, it doesn't always hit the emotional or narrative depth it reaches for.
Visually, the movie is striking. The world-building feels rich and immersive, and the existential questions at the core of the story are compelling. Robert Pattinson brings complexity to the title character, handling the duality and inner conflict with subtlety. The supporting cast adds strength, though not all characters get the attention they deserve.
The pacing can be inconsistent, with moments of brilliance occasionally weighed down by clunky exposition or underdeveloped arcs. It flirts with greatness but doesn't quite maintain the tension or cohesion needed to fully realize its potential.
Still, "Mickey 17" stands out as a unique and entertaining sci-fi experience. It's clever, strange, and visually imaginative-even if its pieces don't always fit together perfectly.

author: siderite
title: A terrible adaption and a tasteless satire
text:
I've read the book and it was fun and light and interesting. The film is none of these. If the book character was emotionally stable and intelligent, Robert Pattinson played it like a mentally challenged person. If the girls in the book were interesting, competent and attractive for very different reasons, in the film they are sexed up junkies. If Mickey's friend was a narcissistic jerk, in the film it was so caricaturesque that he barely felt like a human being. If the exalted leader of the colony was a stuck up bunghole with some hard religious beliefs about printed humans, in the film he's a grotesque parody of Donald Trump. If the aliens in the book were always dangerous and alien, in the film they are fuzzy balls who talk a lot. And so on and so on.
It was all so heavy handed that I couldn't enjoy a thing. The sci-fi parts were minimal, and the human aspects were sketched as by a 10 year old who thinks he's smart. I don't understand what the makers of the movie were trying to achieve. Did they believe that translating something that felt like The Martian or the Bobiverse into a bitter and unsubtle Korean style mock of Christian America was going to be successful? It felt like one of those shows for kids where everybody is psychotic, but somehow little children eat it up.
And it gets worse from here. Some of the parts of the film were unintelligible. The sound was just as poorly treated as the subject of the movie so you couldn't even understand what people were saying. There were no redeeming qualities of any of the shots. Everything was dark and grey and felt cheap.
This film is a mean spirited piece of dung. Why not make your own story if you're going to ignore the original material? I am very disappointed.

author: AvianZoo
title: Don't listen to the haters
text:

Not once was there any doubt in credibility in terms of the locations or the scenes etc, which admittedly is basics for a high-end movie, but bigger films have failed in this aspect whereas this movies does not.

Watched this on a Saturday night, hoping to switch off from the week and to enjoy it while coming out the other side being pleased for having watched it. I can say that this film ticked all those boxes.
Don't listen to the haters, this film is good.

author: xroo-73772
title: Mickey Remembering His Deaths is a Miracle - Not Remembering This Movie is a Blessing.
text:

It makes the clones behave a bit differently. One thing that can never be part of of these backups, obviously, are his deaths. Three minutes into this movie, Mickey 17 is asked: "What does it feel like to die?" It will not be the last time. Everybody thinks that Mickey can remember his deaths - and he can.
This lazy and derisive storytelling is the main characteristic of this preposterous "science fiction" movie. Nothing here does make actual sense. The mean and childish clownworld of a society. Mark Ruffalo's most charmless, ugly and repulsive "charismatic leader" ever. The idea to colonize an ice-planet. Its only two lifeforms: an instantly deadly virus and monster isopods.
The distinctive unworldly undertone calls Bong Joon Ho's "Parasite" to mind - also labeled as "black comedy" -, where a bunch of low-lifes miraculously ace doing rich people stuff, then just regress to their low-life ways. Never before was a social satire that random. Most likely there have been SF-movies as ostentatiously incoherent and illogical as "Mickey 17". Why would anybody care to remember them? "Mickey 17" is a drab, unfunny, overlong isopod of a movie.

author: Barooni_gamer
title: Half-Past 1 & 2
text:
The film starts differently and does a great job in the first half, portraying the degradation of existence caused by the destructive intersection of naive powerful figures and impotent intellectuals, leading to the creation of a hollow, absurd reality. There's a sharp, critical tone reminiscent of Parasite, and I genuinely hoped the film would continue along this path.
However, by the second half, the movie loses its momentum. The introduction of character simulations (Mickey 17 and Mickey 18) could have been a fascinating, thought-provoking element, but it feels wasted and underdeveloped. This shift from a promising start to a predictable, rushed conclusion makes the film feel like it lost its original vision. The first half has clever humor and was meaningful in its exploration, but the second half turns stale.
Instead of building on the sci-fi theme, the movie becomes too derivative, resembling too many other works in the genre. The character relationships feel shallow, the events become outdated, and by the end, there's a sense of disappointment, as if the film had to finish quickly without offering any real creative impact.
Overall, Mickey 17 had the potential to be a modern, humorous sci-fi story, but its failure to fully develop its context ruined much of its promise.

author: bsiginc7
title: amazing concept but terrible execution
text:
Mickey 17 had all the makings of a sci-fi classic. The concept - a disposable human clone sent on dangerous missions, resurrected repeatedly - is bold, thought-provoking, and rich with existential questions. It promised a deep dive into what it means to be human, the value of life, and the loneliness of being endlessly replaceable. Unfortunately, while the premise is stellar, the execution falls painfully flat.
The movie struggles to find a consistent tone, awkwardly swinging between dark comedy, philosophical musings, and flashy action scenes without ever committing to any of them. Key themes that should have been explored with nuance are rushed or glossed over entirely. Instead of building emotional stakes, the film relies heavily on exposition dumps and flashy visuals to move the story along.
Robert Pattinson does his best with the material, bringing some much-needed depth to Mickey's various iterations, but even his performance can't save the clunky dialogue and uneven pacing. Supporting characters feel half-baked, introduced and discarded with little impact. What could have been a gripping exploration of identity and mortality becomes a shallow, confusing mess by the final act.
Visually, Mickey 17 impresses - the world-building and special effects are stunning - but style can't make up for the lack of substance. Ultimately, the movie feels like a wasted opportunity: a brilliant idea sacrificed to weak storytelling.
For a story about endless rebirths, Mickey 17 sadly never comes alive in the way it should.

author: dwoodbiz
title: A Sci-Fi Reflection on Mortality, Morality, and the Myth of Perfection
text:
Mickey 17 is not your standard science fiction fare-it is a cerebral and emotionally charged meditation on identity, sacrifice, and the dangerous delusion of utopia. With a central premise that explores disposable life through the lens of cloning and colonization, the film offers a visually striking and narratively potent reflection on what it means to be human in a universe that views individuality as expendable.
Robert Pattinson delivers a tour de force performance, carrying the weight of existential dread and reluctant heroism with nuance and restraint. His portrayal of Mickey is layered with vulnerability, rebellion, and quiet intelligence-reminding us that humanity is not just in our genes, but in our choices.
The political overtones of the former senator-turned-leader character offer a pointed commentary on modern leadership, evoking unsettling echoes of the current administration. While this allegory is compelling, it occasionally leans too heavily into satire, teetering on the edge of caricature. Still, the metaphor remains clear: when power is consolidated in the pursuit of control, morality becomes malleable-and lives become statistics.
At its core, Mickey 17 grapples with the cost of progress. The film challenges the notion of the "perfect colony," exposing its ethical rot and emotional void. In doing so, it honors the irreplaceable value of a single life. It posits that true civilization is not built by the absence of flaws but by the presence of empathy.
Perhaps its most haunting truth is this: we are all aliens the moment we leave Earth. And in that otherness, we are tasked with humility. The unknown must be approached not with dominance, but with reverence. Not as conquerors, but as guests.
Mickey 17 is a reminder that humanity's future depends not on replication, but on reflection.

author: chloq
title: When all emotions are displayed in one scene
text:
Firstly the movie is definitely good. Pattinson's acting was impressive.
It all starts with the protagonist Mickey falling into the hole while colonising a planet and being chased by alien creatures. After that a black screen and we are presented with the guy's story: his lifestyle, his credits and the chase after him. With no options to escape the mafia he signs a form to participate in the colonisation of a planet hoping to escape the mafia. Without reading the form to the end Mickey agrees to become a clone - a human coloniser who will be used and reprinted if he dies. This is where the main story of the film "Mickey 17" begins.
The film turned out to be not an ordinary film. Sometimes overlong and boring and sometimes impressive so much that you watch it and don't understand how the director came up with it. There is an expression when you can feel all emotions in one scene: from disgust to joy, from sadness to anger - and this is exactly what happens every minute. This is what surprises me the film is very unusual without Hollywood clichés - it is an author's film. It touches on various topics, albeit briefly. Its biggest feature is a black humour satire in the role of the colony's main president an emperor with royal tendencies. In my opinion Mickey himself is very well written. Pattinson is a great actor! He played two different clones perfectly on the same screen. The film was a bit long and a bit boring at times but Pattinson diluted the film perfectly. He didn't get lost in the shots but stood out.
I liked the film for its beauty and the lead actor's performance. But I also didn't like that the film was just unbearable in places - some scenes were avoidable and some of the references were long. The situations were silly and the staging wasn't great. But I enjoyed it nonetheless. I advise everyone to watch this movie!

author: RegalsReelView
title: Life, Space, and Clones
text:
To escape a loan shark and death, Mickey takes a job as an expendable on an intergalactic colonization expedition. Tasked with dangerous and likely fatal jobs, Mickey is cloned after every death. The only thing that has kept him going through his 17th reincarnation is Nasha, the love of his life. Things were going well until Mickey, 17, became a multiple and bumped into Mickey, 18. The existence of multiples is illegal, and they must find a solution before they are discovered and executed.
This science fiction reincarnation tale is fascinating. On the surface, the story seems simple and silly. Clones encounter each other, and things go awry, creating comedy and entertainment. The story is also about more complicated topics like life, death, and ethics, to give a few examples. Along with a thought-provoking, engaging story, the movie has action, idiotic comedy, clones, aliens, and space travel. Unfortunately, the two-hour and seventeen-minute runtime does not fly by at lightspeed, with some parts being slow and unnecessary. Overall, this is an interesting and entertaining movie and should be watched.

author: jakethesnake-18813
title: Messy but entertaining
text: So I've only seen two of Bong Joon-Ho's movies; this and Parasite. Between the two, Parasite is definitely the stronger movie, but this one is a ton of fun as well, even if it is kinda messy. To put into words what works, Robert Pattinson is incredible, simply incredible. He plays both Mickeys extremely well and is able to use the power of his voice to clearly differentiate between them. Now as great as Robert Pattinson is, what holds this movie back is the larger story as a whole. It's not bad, but there's simply too much going on (mostly due to the over abundance of flashbacks) and some of it borders the fine line between satire and parody (large in part thanks to the characters and performances of Mark Ruffalo and Toni Collette). Even further, nothing in this movie really stands out on a technical level. It's not bad, just feels a little cinematically flat. Overall, I like the movie, I find it entertaining, but it's definitely not Bong's best work.

author: zhazha-90461
title: Mickey 17 is an Absolute Disaster
text:
Mickey 17 is a complete mess - probably the worst sci-fi movie I've seen in years. It starts with an interesting premise but quickly spirals into a bizarre, incoherent disaster. None of the actors bring any depth or charisma to their roles, making it impossible to connect with any of the characters. The special effects are underwhelming, far below the standard expected for a modern sci-fi film. author: jp_91
title: "Mickey 17" is a great film that tells a story that is in the process of beginning in real life.
text: Bong Joon Ho returns with his new film "Mickey 17", written by the same director based on the novel "Mickey7" written by Edward Ashton, in this science fiction and dark comedy story tells a story about how expendable human life can be for those who govern us, in addition to using other themes of social denunciation such as colonization (an obvious criticism of the past, the colonization of the American continent) and another more current criticism where the actor Mark Ruffalo plays an ambitious political character who does not care about others, only his ego and being praised by his cult, obviously based on the current president of the United States. Robert Pattinson for his part shows us once again that he is an excellent actor when playing Mickey 17 and Mickey 18, each character with their own personalities. Bong Joon Ho's direction hits the mark, spectacularly handling the actors and the technical crew. The sound design is spectacular, making the viewer feel like a part of the plot; the costume design is wonderful and lavish; the production design is top-notch; the cinematography is incredible, offering visual delight; and the editing creates a dizzying story full of suspense, action, and drama. The special effects are well done in most of the scenes that require them. "Mickey 17" is a great film that tells a story that is in the process of beginning in real life.

author: imdbfan-1770986762

The world-building is immersive, drawing you into a universe that's both awe-inspiring and terrifying in its possibilities. author: CommonSenseCritic
title: Solid Satire
text:
When - 8:10 PM
Where - Indian Lake Regal Cinema
With Who - Myself
First Thoughts -
I will see anything that Bong Joon Ho makes, especially after my introduction to his work with 2019's Parasite. It's clear that in every film he makes, he adds layers upon layers of subtext and metaphors for some of the biggest issues facing humanity today. Bong Joon Ho is the Shrek of movie directors working in present day.
That writing ability is once again on full display here with Mickey 17. With this film, beneath the surface level political satire, is a story that causes the audience to contemplate death, the value of human life, identity, personality, and technological advancement. That being said, the political satire here is very in your face and on the nose, particularly Mark Ruffalo as President Tru, uh, I mean former Congressman Kenneth Marshall. I understand what he was going for, but the obviousness of it very quickly moved away from funny to annoying very quickly. Toni Collette as his wife Ylfa was also terrible, with a really odd focus on "sauce" for some reason that was never explained and or expanded on.
Robert Pattinson has truly come a long way from his Twilight days, now having worked with some of the best, most visionary directors active today. His performances astound me, the sheer range in his abilities from his voice to his physical acting and mannerisms. Pattinson is a master of the acting craft and I'm excited to see where he goes in the future.
Technically, the movie is fine, nothing of note either positively or negatively comes to mind.
Overall, a fun time in spite of a few flaws.
Full Review to follow.

author: WuLiMammoth
title: Original, funny and engaging..until it wasn't.
text:

author: xhsvkky
title: The only 10 is the extra Mickeys from the Book
text:
After having read Mickey7 I was excited to watch a talented director and a brilliant actor tackle one of the most interesting concepts ever put to page.
Instead what you get is just over 2 hours of absolute chaos. The books genius plot is thrown away so that the writer and director can make a few cheap laughs and comment sloppily about the dangers of following charismatic leaders. Unfortunately he is neither charismatic or a leader but a thinly veiled attempt to mix popularism/ religious fanaticism and Macbeth into one very annoying package.
Robert Pattinson does all he can to keep you entertained but with the script he was given even he is struggling to make you care about a single thing that happens on screen.
Part of me wished that I had not read the book beforehand but if I hadn't I am unsure as to whether I would have understood a single thing that was going on. On the other hand I wouldn't have had to sit watching something that made me increasingly more angry with each scene as they threw away every brilliant facet of the novel.
This is an example of how not to adapt a book.

author: spencer-w-hensley
title: Well acted and visually impressive but needlessly confusing and overlong
text:
I had somewhat looked forward to this movie since seeing the trailer but wasn't necessarily in a hurry to rush to theaters for it.
However a friend wanted to go so I joined him.
Unfortunately this movie for me is going to go down as one of the most frustrating movies of the year.
I say frustrating because there is much to admire here. Performances are good the visual effects are very impressive but the movie is extremely confusing and really doesn't need to be in order to convey its message.
That's really my biggest problem with this movie. It's just so confusing and by the time I left the theater I had no idea what the hell was going on or what I just saw.
It's also about 20 minutes too long and really could have users some editing in order to be more effective.
Pattinson is very good as is his supporting cast and I was very impressed by the visuals and set design but this movie is just very exhausting because it just really makes no sense.

author: imdbfan-2387093189
title: Good casting, but becomes repetitive very quickly.
text:
A dark comedy with social commentary. I have nothing against this description by itself, but the "jokes" started to feel repetitive and unfunny really quick. It was all in the same note: Look at Mickey suffering, and check out how much this rich guy sucks! As for the social commentary, I just found it to be nothing new, both in the message itself but also the approach. I think we are done with over the top, almost cartoonish stupid evil rich douchebags. I just think it doesn't add anything new to the discussion if you do it the same way everytime.
This movie was also way less sci-fi than I initially expected. It's sci-fi in theory but in practice it never goes deep enough in any sci-fi related topic to be able to be recommended as a sci-fi movie for anyone interested in that. It barely touches on the deep conversation about the mind and the implications of cloning, which I also found disappointing at best.
The plot was a little bit directionless, with poor focus, as it shifted from one core to another chaotically. I don't think it was the worst thing ever but I would prefer if they had one single core to build upon, such as the contact with the alien race or the battle of survival between the Mickeys.
Lastly, very few characters were fleshed out. Most characters were cartoonish and had their screentime reserved almost exclusively for repetitive jokes. As for the main characters, Mickey 17 was alright, a little bit too reactive for a protagonist, Mickey 18 was great and a lot of fun to watch, and Nasha was "the perfect human being" the entire film, being glazed over nonstop and had no real character beyond that.
Overall, while I think Mickey 17 had its moments (pretty funny ones) and an important message about a dark side of reality, but it hit the same note with the humor until it got boring, didn't innovate on this message at all, had poor focus and bad characters and did not engage in any meaningful sci-fi discussion at all. With the weight of the casting I left the theater very disappointed. The acting was great, though.

author: ethanbresnett
title: A slight let down but still an enjoyable and entertaining film
text:
Bong Joon Ho at the helm. Robert Pattinson playing multiple versions of himself. Mark Ruffalo and Toni Collette chewing as much scenery as they can get their hands on. It all seems like a bit of a slam dunk, but unfortunately, Mickey 17 doesn't quite hit the dizzying heights we've come to expect from Bong Joon Ho.
The film follows down on his luck Mickey, who signs up to be an 'expendable' on a colonisation mission to a far off planet. This essentially means he is repeatedly killed and reprinted in the name of science / health and safety experiments. However, when a variant of Mickey is left alive and another reprinted, complications ensue as they both seek to survive.
Now this seems like a premise that is open to all kinds of fun and interesting commentary, but it feels a little wayward and muddled as the film progresses. The runtime feels a little indulgent as a result, and the whole thing could have been a bit leaner. The shift in focus towards the end of the film felt a little left field, and the body double hijinks takes a bit of a back seat. It almost feels like two very different films mashed together, with varying results.
Visually I think the film is really impressive though, with the set design, costuming, and effects all top notch. The performances are also great, with Pattinson giving a solid performance, and the supporting cast of the likes of Naomi Ackie, Mark Ruffalo, Toni Collette and Steven Yeun all rise to the occasion.
So overall Mickey 17 is an enjoyable albeit slightly muddled affair. Good performances and visuals don't quite make up for a mediocre story, but viewed as a whole it is very watchable and respectable.

author: JuHoE
title: An Interesting Movie Based on the Novel Mickey7
text:
Mickey 17, directed by Bong Joon Ho, brings a fresh take on science fiction with a comedic and thought-provoking narrative. The film follows Mickey Barnes (Robert Pattinson), an "expendable" who is repeatedly resurrected after each death, a concept that allows for both dark humor and deep philosophical questioning. While the movie delivers a great plot and impressive performances, it may struggle under the weight of expectations set by Bong's previous masterpiece, Parasite.
The film's visual style is reminiscent of Snowpiercer, another of Bong's works, but instead of focusing on class struggle, Mickey 17 leans more into political commentary. The futuristic setting, combined with intricate world-building, creates a gripping atmosphere that keeps audiences engaged. However, while the movie successfully balances humor and gore, some scenes-particularly an unnecessary intercourse scene-feel out of place and detract from the overall narrative.
Robert Pattinson's performance is a major highlight, particularly in how he differentiates between Mickey 17 and Mickey 18 through distinct voice changes. His ability to add nuance to both versions of his character enhances the film's exploration of identity and individuality. The movie's quieter moments of gore serve their purpose without being overly gratuitous, fitting well within the tone of the story.
Overall, Mickey 17 is an entertaining sci-fi comedy that offers a mix of political intrigue, dark humor, and strong performances. While it may not reach the legendary status of Parasite, it still stands out as a bold and engaging film worth watching. 7/10.

author: StrickIand
title: A Sci-Fi Saga of Ambition Over Execution
text:
Not good as expected
But still qualified for big screen
1. Overstuffed Themes, Underdeveloped Ideas
The film juggles cloning identity crises, labor exploitation, and dystopian violence but reduces them to surface-level symbolism.
2. Theatricality Over Immersion
Robert Pattinson's exaggerated performance clashes with Bong's signature realism. Stage-like blocking and underwritten side characters create emotional detachment, despite flashes of existential wit.
3. Weak Antagonists, Missed Critique
Villains lack depth, framed as mere "system enforcers" without exposing the oligarchy's mechanisms. Conflicts feel simplistic compared to *Parasite*'s sharp class allegory.
4. Monotonous Visual Language
The gray-toned, icy landscapes-though technically stunning-grow repetitive. Unlike *Parasite*'s layered spaces, the film misses chances to contrast environments for thematic resonance.
5. Misplaced Dark Humor Undercuts Pathos
Bong's trademark satire feels overused: morbid jokes about Mickey's deaths trivialize his existential trauma. Instead of deepening character vulnerability, the humor often reduces his plight to absurdist farce, muddying the emotional core.
6. Clunky Narrative Pacing & Plot Devices
Well. A common problem in sci-fi.

author: sujanfaster
title: A Frivolous Surprise
text:
You want some movies to surprise you despite having certain expectations about them. When I watched the premise of Mickey 17 that is what I had in mind. Although I wasn't a big fan of Parasite I did like the surprise element in the movie and with Bong Joon Ho tying up with Robert Pattinson set my expectations for this movie a tad too high. If not for anything else, I was hoping to walk out with some great visuals and entertainment considering the movie is set in an out of the world theme.
Mickey 17 follows the story of an expendable in outer space being used for different kinds of human experiments. Bong Joon Ho continues with his theme of exploitation of the lower class by the rich in this movie but projects it a bit differently. You cannot help but draw parallels to some of the things that are happening in the world currently in some scenes. Sometimes it is way too obvious that they make the scenes look jarring. The movie chooses to go with over the top portrayal of certain characters and concepts. The problem is that there isn't enough pay off in the end for these choices. The movie could have also been technically better as there aren't really captivating visuals or background score for this type of film.
Movie's narration is primarily laid out by the character design. Robert Pattinson as Mickey Barnes does play a unique role and also speaks in a way we haven't seen him do before. It is refreshing to watch but you also kind of miss the quiet Rob. Mark Ruffalo as Kenneth Marshall is clearly written as a Trump/Republican politician and the character loses its sheen after a few minutes into the movie. Antics played by his character along with his wife played by Toni Colette feel repetitive after a while. Both Mark and Toni seem trying too hard or maybe their character writing isn't good enough. While Steven Yeun's role starts off with a promise, it does not add anything significant to the movie eventually. Other supporting characters seem similar to the character from some of the quirky MARVEL movies. There was a great opportunity for Bong Joon Ho to make an emotional impact with the other world CGI characters but they end up being gags which is a big letdown.
Mickey 17 is another experiment on an already proven concept which is unseriously serious.

author: flartpoop
title: The movie lacks sauce.
text:
Starting from the beginning, the movie decided to interest viewers with an interesting plotline based on continued deaths, (not explored) and an irreverence for life (poorly handled) that would make audiences sympathize with the protagonist, Mickey 17.

Mickey is a kind, naive "expendable", who no one cares for, as a result of unfortunate circumstances spurred on by his own unthinking decisions, which he blames himself for.

The movie begins by detailing the reason we spend most of our time not on Earth and on a foreign planet; Timo and Mickey owe a dangerous man an exorbitant amount of money due to his naivete in investing in a macaron business, (inspired by Timo) and must go off to planet Niflheim to avoid said man. Timo, his only friend, is the one that actually gets him into trouble with loan sharks. Does he apologize for his behavior throughout the movie? No. Does he only betray Mickey's trust at every possible junction? Yes. Does Mickey ever react to this in a meaningful way or change the way he views Timo, even after he was almost brutally murdered by him? I'll let you answer that for yourself.

This movie is one of plot holes, and loose threads, attempting to broach feminism, corruption, discussions of democracy, (and much more), which I would be glad to investigate more if the movie gave itself more time, but after writing this review, I can definitely say the less I think about this movie and the time it wasted with me, the better.

author: madebyiiisa
title: Don't Compare-Just Watch
text:
I LOVED this movie. It completely exceeded my expectations-the trailer didn't do it justice at all. What stood out most was how real and honest it felt. The comedy was natural, never forced, and the acting was incredible. Robert Pattinson, especially, He plays two completely different versions of the same character, and he makes both feel believable and distinct.

author: malmevik77
title: Great themes embedded in dark satire
text:
Mickey 17
Mickey 17 is directed by the same award winning director of Parasite, and it shows. This science fiction dark comedy about the expendable nature of clones digs much deeper into themes of class struggle, political corruption, another story on colonization in the name of religion, drug use and mental illness.
In the near future, human cloning has been discovered, used in such a way that the clones all think they are the original after memories are downloaded into their brains. Naturally, this was quickly used for criminal reasons, and was therefore banned for many reasons. However, a failed politician, with a flair for over the top behavior and bending the truth (remind you of anybody?) leaves Earth to colonize another planet. He brings along the cloning process, used to regenerate people who die in science experiments, to aid in the journey.
This goes dark very quickly. The questions come out: Does each clone have their own soul? Is the soul being artificially duplicated? What happens when 2 clones exist at the same time? All of this is explored as an interesting spin on What Makes Someone Human.
I really liked this film. The Americans as evil colonizers trope is played out, but it did aid in setting up the rest of the brilliant storytelling. The over the top performances by pretty much everybody in the cast kept me laughing even when evidencing horrible behavior. In addition, there are some interesting aspects of character development amongst those whose morality is more gray than black or white.
Keep an open mind, and look for the story that is being told beneath the surface. That's where I found it truly satisfying.

author: RealDanLeahey
title: Enjoyed my watch but feels like it focuses on the wrong material
text:
So i was pretty hyped to see this movie this past weekend. Went with a group of friends and thought it was a pretty enjoyable movie. But nothing ground breaking.
While I did enjoy it I couldnt help but feel like something was wrong. Its taken me days to think about it and I realized what it was. Its that this movie sets up some interesting questions that it doesnt bother to answer.
Instead of being another movie about classism, I think it would have spent its time better diving deeper into the differences between Mickey's 17 and 18. Trying to place an answer to what is it that makes us "Us"? Are we merely a culmination of memories or are we more than that? Is the way Mickey precieves his memories what makes us different?
Ultimately was a fun movie, worth the watch, could have been better.

author: superstradivariusboys
title: Well made, good messages, but not for everyone
text:
Mickey 17 is the kind of movie that sticks with you-for good reasons-but it certainly won't appeal to everyone.
The director presents a vision of the future that feels eerily close to what could be our reality in the next decade or two. Many elements, if not all, paint a terrifying picture of humanity's future. And that's a good thing. The film's dark humor serves as a clever coating for its harsh commentary on human exploitation, violence, racism, secret societies, and more.
The performances are great. Robert Pattinson does an excellent job portraying a "disposable" human, reduced to nothing more than an experiment, endlessly used and discarded. The entire cast delivers strong performances-even when some go a little over the top. But I actually appreciate that, as it mirrors the exaggerated behavior of certain political figures, serving as a stark reminder of the world we live in.
What's truly unsettling is knowing that many people will empathize with the protagonist's suffering in this film while feeling nothing for the real-world victims of war and oppression today. That's one of the movie's strongest messages, and I think it lands well.
Ultimately, Mickey 17 succeeds in delivering its themes with style and originality. It may not be a masterpiece in my eyes, but it's unique enough to stay with me for a long time. The film is also technically impressive, with stunning visuals, an immersive setting, and well-executed VFX.
Great movie. If humanity is still around in 50 years, I believe this one will stand the test of time.
By the way, it's based on the book Mickey7, so if you're a bookworm, you might want to check that out!

author: daisukereds
title: "Like real déjà vu.. but for smell"
text:
This movie could have been about interesting introspection into topics like potential "Immortality", the exploration of the "ship of Theseus" thought experiment, hive minded Aliens, the evolution of human technology and resource intensive advancements, ethics and more.
I'm honestly disappointed..
Both "Mickey 17" and the "Electric State" movies have been considerably-bad adaptations of very interesting books. This one more so because of the man (seemingly) in charge and the expectations behind it.. at least the other showed its colors in the trailers.
It is not just the unnecessary changes, added elements that don't contribute and deviate for no meaningful reason.. but the dialogue is somewhat obnoxious (lots of talking and not much being said), strange performances and a execution that is hard to take seriously. Instead of concerning itself with world-building this sci-fi future (more of a background element), it focused entirely on Mickey and the dumb guy running the expedition.. making it feel somewhat childish. I am not a fan of Robert Pattinson, but he delivers two believable different performances of two annoying and underwritten characters.. and Ruffalo's acting skills are again put into question (2023's Poor Things) by his performance of a clown in a high position.
So, as an adaptation, it's bad..
As a mass-appeal movie? I can see it entertaining some! It's not that deep, has interesting sci-fi elements, and visual appeal.
But even still, it is over two hours of scenes of little importance and with characters that have little to no motivation (making it feel slow in the process), and the story feels like the prologue to a marathon that finished before everyone can start running. I found it very lacking and would deter anyone from watching this in theaters.

author: RobertN1
title: Mickey 17 - Film Review
text:
Mickey 17 is director Bong Joon Ho's highly anticipated follow up project after the release of Parasite. In this story, we follow Mickey (portrayed by Robert Pattinson), a failed businessman who volunteers to be an expendable on Niflheim to get away from a loan shark. Niflheim is a ship run by failed politician Kenneth Marshall (portrayed by Mark Ruffalo) that is on course to establish a new world. As an expendable, Mickey consistently dies and is reborn to be the ships guinea pig.

Like everyone else I was really excited to see this film after watching Parasite. As far as the cinematography goes, the film is beautiful. The ship, other worlds, and 'aliens' are all really well done. I also really liked Mickey as I felt bad for his character and liked the overall concept.

However, the film isn't nearly as good as Parasite. The film doesn't elaborate enough on the relationship between the Mickey's. There is also a love triangle that is briefly mentioned and then totally gets forgotten. I also wish they expanded on the creatures a bit more. I was really interested in them but you never really learn about them.

The film also has a lot of social commentary to today's climate. While they deny Kenneth Marshall is based on Donald Trump/MAGA, it seems to take some inspiration from him (and evangelicals/religious leaders). If that bothers you, this may not be the film for you.

With that being said, I enjoyed the film and would likely watch it again - 7/10.

author: roniluciaofficial
title: Weak links don't ruin experience as a whole
text:
As a long-time fan of both Robert Pattinson and Bong Joon-Ho, I'm obviously biased. This film, as most South-Korean films are, is not for everyone. It's strange, to say the least. But it's strange in one of those wonderful ways that make you feel like a child again. It's like a comic book, or a cartoon. It's absurd, in the best of ways.
Robert Pattinson delivers a performance to be remembered. It's not his best, but it certainly cements him as one of the greats of our generation. This film is to him what "Planet of the Apes" was to Charlton Heston. I stand by that statement.
Surrounding cast, however, is nothing but adequate. The weakest links are definitely Mark Ruffalo and Toni Collette. Their characters look great on paper, with strong motivations and a sense of humor, but both actors look like they don't want to be there. Ruffalo could have done so much with the character he was given, but he turned it into a mockery, in a bad way, and seems like he reallt phoned it in. As for Collette - what can i say. Forgettable as always, just like everything else she's ever done.

author: mathazo
title: A Sci-Fi Snoozefest That Wastes Its Potential
text:
Mickey 17 is a major disappointment, especially given the high expectations surrounding it. The premise is fascinating, and the cast is strong, yet the film manages to be utterly dull from start to finish. The concept had so much potential that I couldn't help but imagine how Christopher Nolan would have handled it-he likely would have turned it into a masterpiece.

Beyond its sluggish pacing, the film is riddled with logical inconsistencies, even within its own fantastical framework. Why does the protagonist fall in love so quickly with someone so unattractive? What do the creatures eat? How have they survived for so long? How do they understand vocabulary related to things they've never encountered? And why is Mickey 17 so drastically different from Mickey 18 when other clones, including the psychopath shown earlier, didn't display such disparities?

These unanswered questions, combined with the film's uninspired execution, make Mickey 17 a frustrating and forgettable experience. A wasted opportunity in every sense.

author: imdbfan-1961931164
title: Very enjoyable
text:
I see some criticisms about this movie, but I think a lot of them are either not based in fact or shouldn't be cause for concern

author: byruineves
title: A Promising Idea That Loses Its Way
text:
Mickey 17 had the potential to be an innovative sci-fi/comedy film, and it starts off in an engaging and original way. However, as the story progresses, it loses focus and ultimately turns into something generic, with an uninspired and rushed conclusion.
Robert Pattinson delivers a solid and well-rounded performance, proving his versatility even in a film that leans more towards comedy - something outside his usual genre. Despite the lighter tone, Pattinson brings depth to his character, making the story feel more grounded and adding an emotional layer to the film that otherwise would feel empty.
Cloning is a fascinating subject for a sci-fi movie because of all the moral and practical dilemmas it presents. Mickey 17 introduces these ideas but doesn't fully engage in them, shifting focus to a less compelling storyline midway through - the Creepers.
It feels out of the place compared to the film's promising start and even the trailers- The initial mix of humor and originality is lost, and by the end, the movie feels like it was hurriedly wrapped up just to deliver something, lacking any real creativity or impact.
That said, the film excels in its production design. The setting and character outfits are well-crafter, adding to the immersive sci-fi atmosphere. Additionally, the visual effects are compelling, bringing the futuristic world to life in a convincing and visually stunning way, which helps maintain engagement even when the story fails to do so.

author: Irene212
title: Multiple Mickeys, multiple motifs
text:
When Mickey 17, Mickey 18, and Nasha have their threesome, I almost applauded. Up until then, Mickey (Robert Pattison) is an 'Expendable,' having signed up to be killed and reproduced endless times to qualify for escape from a nearly uninhabitable Earth. A Caucasian colony is being established on the planet Niflheim, and the only way hapless Mickey can make the cut is as a virtual slave. Depressing stuff as we watch Mickey get killed over and over as the capitalists in charge (Mark Ruffalo and Toni Collette) use him to test their technology and Niflheim's habitat. When MIckey 17 is presumed dead, 18 is created.
Nasha (Naomi Ackie), a security guard, began the affair with Mickey 17 en route to Niflheim, and Mickey 18 joins in. As filmed by DP Darius Khondji, their threesome is more wry and sly than erotic, and it breaks with the early misery to expand the movie into an imaginative satire, introducing multiple motifs, challenging our conceptions of identity, of mutual responsibility, and most eloquently of the word alien. We are primed to be afraid of the Niflheim's native species, dubbed Creepers, which are smartly created to look like overgrown tardigrades (a microscopic invertebrate that can withstand almost any environment)-- fear that reflects the xenophobia humans tend to suffer from.
Pattinson carries the weight of the film with his double performance as two utterly different Mickeys-- there is never a moment's doubt about which is which. But Ruffalo is close to disastrous, mugging his way through his role as if he was in a cartoon. Ultimately, though, "Mickey 17" is a richly rewarding movie, start to finish, and really needs to be seen more than once to appreciate all that Bong Joon Ho has included, thematically and cinematically.

author: Wilot
title: The Creepers Collective
text:
In Mickey 17, the real stars of the film aren't the humans, but the Creepers - an enigmatic, mysterious, and oddly cool species that steal the spotlight every time they're on screen. These creatures bring an eerie yet captivating presence to the film, displaying a calm confidence that contrasts sharply with the human chaos around them.
Robert Pattinson, in the titular role of Mickey, delivers a performance that deserves multiple accolades. His character is thrown into the deep end, and Pattinson dives in headfirst, acting his heart out-not once, but twice. Pattinson's portrayal of a man caught in a relentless cycle of death and rebirth is raw and compelling, a testament to his versatility and depth as an actor.
The juxtaposition of the Creepers' coolness with Mark Ruffalo's over the top portrail of the leader Marshall makes human desperation an intriguing dynamic. Though there are moments of silliness, the film does not shy away from the deeper questions it poses about existence and humanity, making for a thought-provoking watch.

author: mgmead-1
title: One star for Pattinson, and the other star for Pattinson - the rest is fiery trash
text:
Take a core sci-fi premise, the question of consciousness lasting across perfect cloning - blast it into space under the oversight of gratuitously flat renditions of Trump-parody, and throw a little pointless lack of character development, and you get a broken fourth wall that found me aware that I was sitting in the theater saying to my wife, "I don't care."

author: ruche794
title: Minor Overload
text:
Positives: Outstanding performance by Pattinson, overall good pace of the movie, I personally was a fan of the acoustic elements, Dialogues were authentic and the fusion of a Dark Comedy and a Political Sci-fi was spot on for my taste. The movie neatlessly takes is place in Joon Ho's filmography fulfilling his social critical and original perspectives, showing similar aspects of his critique as past works (Okja) but being original.

Negatives: The first third of the movie lays out an original basis for a plot, which loses its track towards the end of the movie. While the politic critique towards capitalism, classfights, space expansion finds its relevance today the movie may feel overloaded with different angles of ethical issues. While initially focussing on the perspective of human cloning this lead does not find its deserved perspective by "exploding the cloning device". Overall the unique initial angles fade out to a more standard coloniser vs colonised plot. I also slightly disliked the one dimensional villains for the plot but this is a personal preference.

author: gbill-74877
title: Fantastic
text:
This film had a premise that reminded me of the short stories by George Saunders, those showing technology being used in dehumanizing ways by people at the top of the dog eat dog capitalist pyramid but at the bottom of having basic empathy for others, and I loved that about it. Mark Ruffalo's character is a wealthy racist who babbles empty faith to his acolytes, has no social awareness, and craves constant attention, obviously modeled after Trump/Musk and a reminder that those really pioneering space may not be the noble ones among humanity. Meanwhile there is probably no sharper critique of how some people are treated in this world than the job title Robert Pattinson's character has, which is "Expendable." He's a guy who out of desperation has signed himself up to being used as a human guinea pig, subjected to lethal testing and regularly dying, only to be re-created each time by a 3D printer with 2054 technology.
Bong Joon-ho gives us science fiction, social commentary, and comedy, and while the last one suffered from characterizations that got a little cartoonish, this was a case of two out of three ain't bad, even if I would have preferred a more serious tone throughout. It reminded me a little of Okja and aside from the cool creature design, I loved the strain of respecting all life forms (like not making sauces out of them). The trajectory this was on became apparent eventually so you could quibble with the ending, but along the way it was unpredictable, and I always got the feeling that Bong was enjoying entertaining me. He put some very silly things next to some very dark things and blended some genres together which is dangerous, but for me it worked, I really enjoyed seeing this.

author: colphughes
title: I expected more
text: Great cast, great premise and great potential for a great story that missed the mark. The flashback at the beginning could have been less tell and more show to draw us into Mickey's plight. In fact it was so slow that I considered leaving to go watch something else, before it was able to bring us up to date. I stuck with it, but it never really paid off. The multiples seemed like a missed opportunity, switching instead to focus more on the slightly satirical take on current politics. While there were some stand out parallels - it was clear who Ruffalo's character was meant to be - it almost felt like satire and "dark comedy" were left be the wayside. If there was indeed a political message, it was lost on me.

author: sinscopefilms
title: Decent
text:
Mickey 17 takes a bold sci-fi concept and turns it into a visually interesting but uneven experience. The soundtrack and the sound design are highlights, creating a pleasant atmosphere to the film's mood.
However, the introduction didn't hook me at all and was the weakest part of the film. It felt overwhelming, with too much narration and not enough engagement, except for the body printing sequence. The 2nd act introduces new developments that finally made the story more engaging. Cinematography, while functional, is nothing groundbreaking.
Robert Pattinson delivers a fantastic performance, capturing Mickey's clumsiness and curiosity. Pattinson carries the film with multiple versions of himself, showing distinct personalities in a way that's sometimes incredible. Naomi Ackie also gives a strong performance, adding emotional weight to the story.
The film introduces some interesting world-building elements and its emphasis on efficiency, yet I felt that there are missing explanations to make the story complete.
Visually, the color composition is well-executed, but the sheer number of characters feels overcrowded. The jokes are hit or miss. While the idea of human printing is thought-provoking, it doesn't fully deliver in terms of character development.
This film provides thematic familiarity with the film that feels like a mix between Arrival (alien interactions), The Hunger Games (authoritarian control) and Wall-E (themes of connection and adaptation).
Mickey 17 presents an interesting sci-fi premise with strong performances and great sound design, but its uneven pacing and lack of deeper context hold it back. While it has engaging moments, it struggles to keep that momentum throughout. Overall, decent, but not mind-blowing.

author: vitalymakievsky
title: Original, funny, thought-provoking, and terrifying!
text:
Right out of the gate I figured Mickey 17 must be based on a book. It just has that feel of a good book, where the reader or viewer in this case, is challenged to think instead of being spoon fed.
It a hard to really explain the concept and themes of this movie without spoiling it. But it has all the elements of a good satirical novel and hard-core sci-fi elements often reserved for independent films and books. I was quite surprised that Mickey 17 was produced by a major studio, they really took some risks, and went away from your typical cash grab formula. I can name some themes explored in Mickey 17:
1. The problem of consciousness
2. Nietzschien idea of master slave relationship and ideas of superman
Political ideologies not current political commentary
(There isn't any cloning in this movie, Mickey is a biological copy)
I highly recommend this film to anyone who enjoys books by Kirt Vonnegut, and just loves deep dive sci-fi movies forcing you to reexamine the ideas of technology and ethics.
For the casual viewer, I still highly recommend it, just don't expect the characters to be black or white, and the concepts fully explained. This film expects you to be familiar with some ideas presented and gives explanations rather subtly as compared to more wide audience designed movies. So, it's worth a few views, or watch a YouTube explanation afterwards.
Lastly, in case you're a MAGA-person, don't let a few poor reviews throw you off that Mickey 17, makes fun of Trump. There is only one very short scene depicting hardcore MAGA fanatics. The main villain is nothing like Trump, if anything he is more of an incompetent Hitler type character, with a mix what's wrong with the political system at large.
Enjoy!

author: JoeErie
title: I like weird movies, but I didn't like this
text:
I like some of Bong Joon Ho's other movies (Memories of Murder, The Host, Parasite), and I lile many of Robert Pattinson's films (Cosmopolis, The Rover, Good Time, The Lighthouse, and I like sci-fi movies in general. However, I just didn't like this at all.

Ok, I get that it's supposed to be a satire, but it tries to be funny, and it just isn't. Mark Ruffalo's character reminded me of Trump, which is s really tired comparison these days (as if we don't get enough), and there are many strong female roles - which is not a bad thing, but alongside Robert Pattinson's character, which is an oddly understated and a near "stupid" persona - a character who willingly gets thrown under the bus to die in an almost (but not quite, less amusingly) Brazil-esque way, I find the symbolism here somewhat unsettling.

Was it intentional to make the white male hetereo character repeating cannon fodder, or an accident? Either way it doesn't really work, as I didn't feel the emotional sympathy was genuine, nor was it funny enough to warrant a laugh. I like Pattinson, but I did get a little tired of seeing his super ripped chest.

Then let's get to the next problem, which is how the story you've seen in the trailer basically ends halfway through, in favor of an almost (but not quite) Snuffleupagus-type indigenous monster that is more Sesame Street than Star Trek.

If that whole turn of the story was to make a point about colonization, well that's a stretch considering the marketing campaign I've witnessed for this movie.

I don't know how this compares to the book, but superficially I felt a little funny that the original title is Mickey 7 - not 17. Well, what's new I guess? Nothing here, unfortunately.

author: pzftryzc

author: IISebastianR
